At NiCE, we don’t limit our challenges. We challenge our limits. Always. We’re ambitious. We’re game changers. And we play to win. We set the highest standards and execute beyond them. And if you’re like us, we can offer you the ultimate career opportunity that will light a fire within you.

Change Management & Evangelist, AI Incubation (SPARK)

SPARK | CX International Internal Incubation Team | Location: Pune

So, what’s the role all about?

NiCE is building SPARK, a new internal incubation team that turns great ideas from across CX International into working AI solutions, and then into enterprise-grade tools that roll out to colleagues around the world. A tool only creates value if people use it, so we need a change leader who can make AI feel useful, safe, and exciting.

As Change Management & Evangelist, you will lead the people side of everything SPARK delivers - preparing teams for change, building AI confidence and skills, and creating the energy that turns a new tool into a new habit. You bring a consulting background, so you know how to diagnose, structure, influence, and deliver, and how to tell a story that moves senior leaders and front-line teams alike.

You will be a visible champion of AI for CX International. You will demo, teach, listen, and bring what you hear back to the builders. You will work closely with the Project Manager, the Business Analyst, the AI Architects & Builders, and the Support Helpdesk, Field Sales Enablement team, HR Business Partners.

How will you make an impact?

You will own adoption for every SPARK solution, from the first conversation with the business through to sustained use at scale and be the voice of SPARK across the organization.

Plan and Lead Change



- Assess change impact and readiness for each solution, and map stakeholders, concerns, and the behaviours that need to shift

- Serve as the primary on-the-ground team leader for SPARK initiatives, providing hands-on support throughout rollout and adoption phases.

- Build and run change, communications, and rollout plans for each global launch, tailored to regions, roles, and time zones

- Work with the Project Manager so change milestones sit inside the delivery plan, not after it

- Address resistance and concerns openly, including questions about roles and job security, with honest and consistent messages

Build AI Fluency and Skills

- Design and deliver role-based training, workshops, office hours, and self-paced content that teach people to use SPARK solutions in their own workflow

- Create and maintain the SPARK playbook: guides, templates, FAQs, and good-practice examples

- Promote responsible and secure use of AI, in line with company guidance

- Be in constant engagement with key stakeholders and users to identify engagement roadmap

Be the Evangelist

- Tell the SPARK story through demos, showcases, town halls, and internal roadshows that show what is possible and what is already working

- Build and run a network of AI champions across business units who help their peers adopt new tools and share what works

- Collect ideas from across the organisation and encourage colleagues to bring them to SPARK

- Act as a trusted adviser to senior leaders on how to lead their teams through AI-enabled change

- Draft and send communications as required for CX International, ELT as project sponsor working with NiCE Comms team and HR.

Measure and Improve Adoption

- Define adoption and value measures: active use, depth of use, sentiment, behavior change, and benefits realized

- Run feedback loops with users, the Support Helpdesk, and the architects, turning recurring issues and requests into improvements

- Report adoption progress and lessons learned to sponsors, CX International Senior Leadership and steering committees

Have you got what it takes?

- Bachelor’s degree in business, Organisational Development, Communications, Technology, or a related field, or equivalent experience

- 12-18 years of experience in change management, transformation, or enablement, including a background in management or technology consulting

- Proven record of leading change for technology rollouts and shifts in ways of working, across multiple regions or business units

- Strong knowledge of structured change approaches such as Prosci ADKAR, Kotter certification, or equivalent

- Excellent storytelling, facilitation, and presentation skills, including with senior executives

- Experience designing and delivering training and enablement programs for non-technical audiences

- Hands-on fluency with generative AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, or Copilot, and a practical sense of what they can and cannot do

- Experience in using Notebook LLM, Synthesia, Beautiful.ai or equivalent.

- Ability to influence across teams without direct authority, and to use data to show progress

- Fluency in English

You will have an advantage if you also have:

- Experience in software, SaaS, or technology companies or working for consulting company

- Agentic AI adoption project outside of India is a plus

- Experience running AI or digital champion networks

- Prosci ADKAR or an equivalent change management certification

- Instructional design or learning and development experience

- Experience speaking at internal or external events

- Experience working with teams across APAC, EMEA, and the Americas

What’s in it for you?

SPARK is a chance to be a founding member of a brand-new team, and to shape how NiCE turns AI ideas into everyday tools used by colleagues around the world.

Join an ever-growing, market-disrupting, global company where the teams, comprised of the best of the best, work in a fast-paced, collaborative, and creative environment! As the market leader, every day at NiCE is a chance to learn and grow, and there are endless internal career opportunities across multiple roles, disciplines, domains, and locations. If you are passionate about AI, innovative at heart, and excited to constantly raise the bar on what intelligent technology can do, you may just be our next NiCEr!

Enjoy NiCE-FLEX!

At NiCE, we work according to the NiCE-FLEX hybrid model, which enables maximum flexibility: 2 days working from the office and 3 days of remote work, each week. Naturally, office days focus on face-to-face meetings, where teamwork and collaborative thinking generate innovation, new ideas, and a vibrant, interactive atmosphere.

israel.description:
At NiCE, we don’t limit our challenges. We challenge our limits. Always. We’re ambitious. We’re game changers. And we play to win. We set the highest standards and execute beyond them. And if you’re like us, we can offer you the ultimate career opportunity that will light a fire within you.

So what's the role all about?

The Senior Trust Analyst — UK Sovereign sits at the intersection of security, sales, and customer success, serving as the primary trust and security point of contact for our UK Sovereign customers. This role owns the response to customer security inquiries and questionnaires, supports contract reviews on security and privacy terms, and acts as a trusted advisor on the security posture of our UK Sovereign environments.

In addition to traditional Trust Analyst responsibilities, this role serves as the dedicated liaison between UK Sovereign technical security teams and customers, ensuring transparency, trust, and proactive communication. The Senior Trust Analyst will track and report vulnerability remediation activities in a structured Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) format, deliver regular security status updates, and translate complex technical information into clear, customer-ready communications.

This is a senior, customer-facing position critical to building and sustaining trust with UK government and regulated sector customers, accelerating deal cycles, and reinforcing the integrity of our UK Sovereign security program.

How will you make an impact?

Customer Trust & Security Engagement

- Trusted Advisor: Serve as the primary point of contact for UK Sovereign customers on all matters related to security posture, vulnerabilities, remediation activities, and trust documentation.

- Security Questionnaires: Support end-to-end responses to customer and prospect security questionnaires (SIG, CAIQ, VSA, MoD/UK government questionnaires, and bespoke enterprise formats), ensuring accurate, timely, and consistent answers tailored to UK Sovereign context.

- Responder: Help respond to inbound customer security inquiries via email and ticketing, translating technical controls into clear business language for both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

- Trust Portal & Documentation: Maintain the public trust center and UK Sovereign customer-facing documentation, ensuring security whitepapers, certifications, and standard responses remain current and reusable.

Security Posture & Vulnerability Reporting

- Security Posture Assessment: Collaborate closely with UK Sovereign technical and engineering teams to understand and assess the current security posture of UK Sovereign environments.

- POA&M Reporting: help support vulnerability remediation status in a structured Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) format, documenting identified vulnerabilities, planned remediation steps, responsible parties, target completion dates, and progress against agreed timelines.

- Monthly Customer Reporting: help prepare and deliver monthly security status updates to UK Sovereign customers, including progress on scheduled remediation items and key security metrics.

- Remediation Oversight: Monitor and track remediation activities across engineering and security teams, ensuring alignment with agreed timelines and compliance requirements.

Audit

- Audit Interpretation: Read and interpret third-party audit reports (SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, penetration test summaries) and represent findings to customers in questionnaires and security responses.

Communication & Stakeholder Management

- Information Translation: Gather detailed technical information from engineering and security teams, then convert and filter it into clear, concise, and structured updates accessible to both technical experts and non-technical stakeholders.

- Customer Meetings: participate in security review meetings, capture feedback and action items, and ensure timely follow-up and resolution by technical teams.

- Cross-Functional Coordination: Coordinate input from internal teams to validate questionnaire answers and resolve gaps between stated controls and operational reality.



Have you got what it takes?

- Citizenship & Clearance: UK citizenship and ability to pass and maintain SC clearance.

- Experience: 5+ years in a security, GRC, trust, or technical customer-facing role, with direct ownership of security questionnaires, customer inquiries, and security reporting.

- Questionnaire Expertise: Hands-on experience responding to SIG, CAIQ, VSA, and bespoke enterprise/government security questionnaires.

- Compliance Knowledge: Working knowledge of Cyber Essentials Plus, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and at least one of PCI DSS, GDPR/UK GDPR, HIPAA, or FedRAMP.

- Technical Expertise: Strong technical understanding of security principles, architecture, and vulnerability management, including access control, encryption, incident response, network security, and secure SDLC.

- Cloud & SaaS: Familiarity with cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and SaaS security models.

- Communication: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to translate complex technical controls for non-technical audiences (procurement, legal, executives, government stakeholders).

- Customer Relations: Proven experience in customer-facing roles within security or technology sectors, ideally including regulated or government customers.

- Organisational Skills: Demonstrated ability to manage a high-volume queue, set priorities, and drive multi-stakeholder responses to deadline.

- Education: Bachelor's degree in a relevant field, or equivalent practical experience.

- Discretion: Proven ability to handle confidential customer and company information with integrity and discretion.

You will have an advantage if you also have

- Professional cybersecurity certifications (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CISA, CCSK, ISO 27001 Lead Auditor, Security+).

- Experience working with UK Sovereign, MoD, or UK government environments.

- Familiarity with POA&M processes and structured vulnerability remediation reporting.

- Experience with trust portal platforms (ServiceNow, Whistic, Vanta Trust, Drata Trust).

- Familiarity with AI/ML security and emerging frameworks (NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001).

- Previous leadership or line management experience.

- Integrity and discretion when handling sensitive customer and government information.

- Resilience and adaptability in dynamic, high-pressure regulated environments.

- Proactive, self-motivated, and committed to continuous improvement.

- Fast learner with a demonstrated ability to self-educate on new technologies, products, and evolving security frameworks.

- Collaborative working style across technical, legal, sales, and customer-facing teams.

How will you make an impact?

- Demonstrate deep subject matter expertise in our core technologies, as well as at least one other technology specialty, and develop expertise in a second area of specialty.

- Effectively mentor colleagues on their communication, troubleshooting, process, product knowledge and case work.

- Encourage productive debate and discussion with colleagues to more thoroughly analyse and resolve problems.

- Be influential in improving procedures and processes that improve our efficiency and effectiveness.

- Ensure that each case that you own is progressing according to the response and resolution targets as specified in our Service Level Agreements (SLA). Assist colleagues in accelerating their cases toward timely resolution.

- Provide root cause correction, not just symptom relief. Ensure that all facets of the problem are evaluated to eliminate the recurrence of the issue. Exemplify tenacity in resolving core issues that fully resolve problems and assist peers in doing the same.

- Proactively manage personally assigned and cases from the queue based upon severity and priority of each issue and your skills and ability to resolve.

- Open and monitor incidents created with 3rd party providers. Work with other internal stakeholders to improve our interactions and success in handling these incidents.

- Obtain and maintain certification as a Knowledge-Cantered Service (KCS) Publisher, create useful knowledge content, and update existing knowledgebase articles using KCS methodology. Provide coaching to others on KCS best practices.

Expert at reading and analysing network and other technical diagrams to aid in problem diagnosis and resolution and often provide mentoring to colleagues to improve their technical abilities.

- Provide training to colleagues in real time as you perform your work and assist them in being successful in their roles. Develop training materials, best practice documentation, and other resources that will help others, including customers, to be more successful with our products.

- While a consistent work schedule is a norm, the ability to work a flexible schedule and provide on-call services is needed from time to time.

- Minimum of three years of experience working with and advanced knowledge of technologies such as SaaS, telecommunications, contact centre software, networking technologies such as VOIP, QoS SIP, APIs, BOTs TCP/IP, HTTP, HTTPS, SFTP, scripting, load balancers, proxies, firewalls, and Relational Databases (MSSQL, Oracle, MySQL).

- Time management skills that allow you to work in a highly influential manner in an interrupt-driven environment. Ability to multi-task and maintain professional composure during stressful situations, prioritizing your activities appropriately.

- Superior analytical and problem-solving skills while managing diverse and complex issues in high-pressure, complex, multi-platform/system/vendor environments.

israel.title: Additive Manufacturing Specialist
israel.description:
Vast is developing next-generation space stations and space infrastructure using an incremental, hardware-rich, and low-cost approach. Vast is rapidly developing its multi-module Haven Station to ensure a continuous human presence in space for America and its allies, enabling advanced microgravity research and manufacturing, and unlocking a new space economy for government, corporate, and private customers. Haven Demo’s 2025 success made Vast the only operational commercial space station company to fly and operate its own spacecraft. Next, Haven-1 is expected to become the world’s first commercial space station when it launches in 2027, followed by additional Haven modules. Additionally, the company recently announced Vast Satellite, a high-power satellite product line leveraging its space station components and the heritage of Haven Demo.

Headquartered in Long Beach, California, and with more than 1,000 employees and over a billion dollars in private capital, Vast has built the facilities required to manufacture and operate America’s next space station. The company plans to develop future habitats and systems for the Moon and Mars, dedicated space stations for government partners, and other crewed systems that will unlock the expanding long-term space economy.

Vast is looking for an Additive Manufacturing Specialist, reporting to the Supervisor, Manufacturing, to support the development of the systems that will be required for the design and build of human-rated space stations. You will be responsible for the operation and maintenance of the additive manufacturing equipment, the design of fixturing, and the improvement of additive workflows, as well as part post-processing and quality control.

This will be a full-time, non-exempt position located in our Long Beach location.

Responsibilities:

- Plan and set up print jobs. Verify machine parameters, build layouts, and material settings against qualified processes. Monitor builds and make recovery decisions

- Diagnose build failures and process deviations, identify root causes, and recommend corrective actions

- Design, build, validate, and release fixtures and tooling for builds, post-processing, and inspection. Document them with drawings and revision control

- Map and improve workflows from build prep through post-processing, inspection, and release. Track metrics such as cycle time, throughput, first-pass yield, and machine utilization

- Safely handle and track metal powder, including sieving, loading, de-powdering, storage, and lifecycle control

- Perform and schedule preventive maintenance and troubleshoot equipment

- Operate post-processing equipment such as drills, grinders, CNC, and EDM as required

- Perform verifications and keep complete build, test, fixture, and maintenance records

- Write and refine work instructions, SOPs, and safety practices

- Support rapid iteration and development testing with engineering

- Train cross-functional partners and technicians on equipment, procedures, and safe powder handling

Minimum Qualifications:

- High school degree or equivalency certificate

- 5+ years of hands-on metal additive experience (LPBF) and powder handling or similar environment

- CAD proficiency (e.g., Siemens NX or equivalent)

- Comfortable with hand tools and measurement equipment, and able to follow detailed procedures exactly and safely

Preferred Skills & Experience:

- 9+ years experience of hands-on metal additive experience and powder handling or similar environment

- Ability to read engineering drawings, including GD&T, and work from controlled documentation

- Experience working in aerospace or defense manufacturing environments

- Experience with CNC machining, EDM, or work-holding setup and programming

- Experience with lean or continuous-improvement methods, root-cause analysis, and corrective action

- Experience writing or revising SOPs and work instructions

- Experience with powder quality testing and control

- Experience training or mentoring others

- Excellent written and verbal communication

- Initiative and a record of helping the team raise its standards

Additional Requirements:

- Willingness to work overtime, or weekends to support critical mission milestones

- Ability to lift up to 50 lbs unassisted

- Ability to work with metal powders using appropriate PPE

Pay Range: California
$46.91—$66.59 USD

We calibrate level and compensation to the selected candidate's experience and demonstrated capability. We welcome applicants across a range of experience levels to apply.

You will not be inheriting a factory, a set of procedures, or a test stand — you will be building them. You own how a Vast satellite gets physically built, integrated, and proven flightworthy, from the first development unit through a production line that has to turn out flight hardware at rate.

You will write the integration flow and the test philosophy, stand up the environmental test capability and the ground support equipment, lead the campaigns that use them, and then feed what you learn back into the design so the next ten units build faster than the last. You'll do this working directly alongside the discipline leads for structures, avionics, thermal, power, GNC, and flight software.

If you want to define how spacecraft get built at a company rather than execute someone else's definition of it, this is that job.

Responsibilities:

Integration & Test

- Lead and own integration and test campaigns at every level of spacecraft development — component, box, subsystem, and full vehicle

- Define the test philosophy for the bus: what gets acceptance tested, what gets protoqualified, what qualifies by similarity, and how that philosophy holds up as we move from a one-off development unit to rate production

- Develop acceptance, qualification, and R&D test plans for spacecraft systems, and drive them through execution and closure

- Work with systems and subsystems leads to defining requirements and the verification and validation plans that close them

- Develop, maintain, and operate environmental test systems — random vibration, TVAC, thermal cycling, EMI/EMC, mass properties

- Design, build, and maintain mechanical and electrical ground support equipment (MGSE/EGSE) and the facilities that house it

- Interface with ground test software, implement flight software configuration changes for test, and work hands-on with hardware-in-the-loop test systems

- Own test data: what we record, how it's reviewed, what constitutes a pass, and how results get back to the responsible engineer

Assembly & Manufacturing

- Partner with Design Engineering to drive Design for Manufacture and Design for Test into the bus while the design is still moving — access, fastener reach, connector orientation, test point availability, handling and lift points

- Design, procure, install, and validate assembly, test, and verification processes, including the tooling, fixtures, and work instructions behind them

- Support development builds to surface early learnings and retire integration risk ahead of production ramp

- Triage and diagnose failures, run deep technical investigations, and determine the path forward — containment, risk mitigation, and root cause resolution

- Drive process improvements across manufacturing, test, and integration, with an explicit eye toward repeatability across many identical vehicles

- Contribute to change management, assessing the risk and impact of design or process changes on build and test

- Plan and specify the integration facility footprint as the program scales — clean room, integration bay, test cell, and the flow between them

- Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical discipline

- 8+ years of experience in test engineering, integration, or another hands-on hardware engineering role

- Hands-on experience with spacecraft or complex flight hardware integration.

- Experience with environmental testing, including thermal vacuum and random vibration

- Experience developing and executing test plans and procedures from scratch, and writing the technical documentation that supports them (procedures, test reports, requirements, discrepancy reports)

- Proficiency with at least one of C, C++, Python, or MATLAB for test automation, data reduction, or GSE control

- Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot hardware failures under schedule pressure and drive them to root cause

- Comfortable operating without an established process

Preferred Skills & Experience:

- Able to obtain a security clearance

- Master's or PhD in electrical, electronics, mechatronics, aerospace, or another engineering discipline

- Strong working knowledge of satellite subsystems (C&DH, ADCS, EPS, COMM) and how they come together at the vehicle level

- Experience with multi-unit or constellation builds, where the integration flow has to be repeatable across 10+ identical vehicles rather than optimized for one

- Clean room operations and ESD-sensitive hardware handling experience

- Hands-on with electrical test equipment (PSU, oscilloscope, DMM, spectrum analyzer)

- Experience designing and implementing automated test systems for electronics

- Understanding of sensors, signal conditioning, and data acquisition electronics

- Familiarity with spacecraft harness design, build, and test best practices

- 3D CAD proficiency, preferably NX

- RF testing and hardware-in-the-loop testing experience

- Familiarity with IPC/J-STD workmanship standards and IPC Class 3 space applications

- Launch site or launch campaign experience

- Ability to work in a clean room environment and around ESD-sensitive hardware

israel.title: Director, Satellite Business International | Directeur(trice), Développement Commercial International - Satellites
israel.description:
Vast is developing next-generation space stations and space infrastructure using an incremental, hardware-rich, and low-cost approach. Vast is rapidly developing its multi-module Haven Station to ensure a continuous human presence in space for America and its allies, enabling advanced microgravity research and manufacturing, and unlocking a new space economy for government, corporate, and private customers. Haven Demo’s 2025 success made Vast the only operational commercial space station company to fly and operate its own spacecraft. Next, Haven-1 is expected to become the world’s first commercial space station when it launches in 2027, followed by additional Haven modules. Additionally, the company recently announced Vast Satellite, a high-power satellite product line leveraging its space station components and the heritage of Haven Demo.

Headquartered in Long Beach, California, and with more than 1,000 employees and over a billion dollars in private capital, Vast has built the facilities required to manufacture and operate America’s next space station. The company plans to develop future habitats and systems for the Moon and Mars, dedicated space stations for government partners, and other crewed systems that will unlock the expanding long-term space economy.

Vast recherche un(e) Directeur(trice), Développement Commercial International - Satellites, sous la responsabilité du SVP, Satellite Business Development & Commercialization, pour diriger le développement commercial axé sur le commerce (communications, observation de la Terre, détection, défense et applications de calcul en orbite) et les gouvernements internationaux pour Vast Satellites. Ce rôle est centré sur les marchés hors États-Unis — notamment l'Europe, le Moyen-Orient et l'Asie — et dirigera l'engagement client, le développement des opportunités, la stratégie de capture, l'engagement gouvernemental/défense et les efforts de partenariat qui font progresser les initiatives de Vast pour développer, fabriquer et exploiter des plateformes de bus satellites avancées.

Il s'agit d'une petite équipe commerciale fondatrice de haut niveau : le rôle exige à la fois des instincts de « hunter » en développement commercial (créer des marchés et de la demande là où il n'en existe pas encore) et des compétences avérées de « closer » (négocier et exécuter des contrats allant de quelques millions à des centaines de millions de dollars).

Ce poste sera à temps plein, exempté, ouvert à un lieu de travail international flexible comme décrit ci-dessus.

Responsabilités :

- Élaborer et exécuter une stratégie globale de marché commercial et gouvernemental international couvrant l'Europe, le Moyen-Orient et l'Asie, alignée sur les objectifs commerciaux de Vast.

- Établir et maintenir une veille stratégique sur le marché et la concurrence concernant les clients spatiaux commerciaux et gouvernementaux internationaux, en distinguant le positionnement de Vast de celui de ses concurrents dans chaque région.

- Piloter la planification interne pour la priorisation des opportunités internationales, la stratégie de capture et le développement du pipeline sur de multiples marchés alliés et partenaires.

- Diriger l'engagement client à travers l'identification d'opportunités, la définition du périmètre des missions, les présentations de capacités et le développement de concepts précoces avec les opérateurs commerciaux internationaux, les sociétés d'observation de la Terre, les ministères de la défense et les entités gouvernementales.

- Tirer parti d'un solide réseau préexistant de haut niveau au sein de la chaîne de valeur internationale de l'espace et de la défense pour ouvrir des portes auprès de clients potentiels et identifier précocement les menaces concurrentielles.

- Diriger l'élaboration des propositions et coordonner les contributions interfonctionnelles des équipes d'ingénierie, de gestion de programme, de finance, juridique et de contrôle des exportations/conformité, avec le soutien de l'analyste BD et de l'ingénieur avant-vente de l'équipe.

- Assumer la responsabilité du développement du pipeline, des prévisions et des rapports pour tous les comptes commerciaux et gouvernementaux internationaux.

- Négocier et conclure des contrats pour des missions commerciales et gouvernementales/défense internationales et les services associés, en naviguant à travers divers cadres nationaux de passation de marchés, de contrôle des exportations (ex. ITAR/EAR) et de partenariat.

- Se coordonner avec l'équipe de sécurité nationale de Vast lorsque les programmes internationaux croisent des parties prenantes ou des enjeux liés au gouvernement américain.

- Représenter Vast lors d'événements de l'industrie spatiale, aérospatiale et de défense internationale en Europe, au Moyen-Orient et en Asie.

- Faire des présentations, participer à des panels et fournir des briefings de haut niveau/C-suite communiquant les capacités et la valeur des plateformes satellites de Vast aux audiences commerciales, gouvernementales et de défense internationales.

Qualifications Minimales :

- Plus de 12 ans d'expérience pertinente dans le développement commercial spatial/aérospatial, les ventes, la gestion de capture ou les contrats gouvernementaux/défense, avec un succès avéré en Europe, au Moyen-Orient et/ou en Asie.

- Historique avéré d'origination et de conclusion personnelle de contrats, y compris des transactions de plusieurs dizaines de millions de dollars ou plus.

- Relations établies et vérifiables avec des clients potentiels au niveau cadre et exécutif, et connaissance du paysage concurrentiel sur de multiples marchés spatiaux et de défense internationaux.

- Expérience dans la chaîne de valeur spatiale/aérospatiale (lancement, bus satellite, charge utile, intégration maître d'œuvre ou opérations), idéalement complémentaire des opérations satellites — par ex. observation de la Terre ou défense internationale.

- Compréhension approfondie des structures de passation de marchés et de partenariat gouvernementales internationales pertinentes pour les programmes d'espace et de défense.

- Solides compétences techniques et capacité à communiquer des systèmes complexes à des audiences commerciales, de défense et gouvernementales internationales.

- Excellentes capacités de communication, d'analyse, de collaboration et de relations interpersonnelles ; à l'aise pour opérer à travers diverses cultures et langues.

- Capacité à opérer de manière autonome, à hiérarchiser les priorités efficacement et à gérer simultanément plusieurs projets internationaux dans un environnement de petite équipe au rythme soutenu.

Compétences et Expériences Souhaitées :

- Relations et crédibilité établies en Europe, au Moyen-Orient et en Asie.

- Maîtrise des langues pertinentes pour les marchés cibles (français, arabe, japonais, etc.).

- Expérience de travail aux côtés d'équipes d'affaires publiques locales ou coordination avec celles-ci (ex. affaires publiques gouvernementales françaises/UE).

- Connaissance des régimes de contrôle des exportations (ITAR/EAR) dans les programmes de satellites internationaux.

Exigences Supplémentaires :

- Capacité à voyager plus de 50 % du temps.

Le/la titulaire contribuera aux travaux de recherche, au développement de partenariats, à la préparation de propositions, à l’organisation d’événements et à la coordination de projets, en appui aux deux directeurs.

Si vous souhaitez participer concrètement au développement des vols spatiaux habités commerciaux, en collaboration avec les agences, les gouvernements et l’industrie, et que vous êtes à l’aise dans la gestion simultanée de plusieurs projets, ce poste est fait pour vous.

Principales responsabilités

- Développer et maintenir une vision structurée de l’écosystème industriel européen pertinent pour Vast : fournisseurs, capacités, expertises nationales, pôles de compétences et partenaires potentiels dans les États membres.

- Préparer des notes de recherche ciblées, études de marché et documents de référence en amont des réunions clients, des propositions et des négociations.

- Gérer la préparation des propositions, offres et réponses aux appels d’offres institutionnels, incluant la recherche, la rédaction et la coordination des contributions des équipes du siège de Vast et des partenaires européens.

- Expérience avec un logiciel CRM ( Salesforce ou outil similaire)  ainsi qu’avec des outils de recherche, de veille ou de constitution de listes de prospects/partenaires.

israel.title: Project Manager, Human Spaceflight and Satellites | Chef de projet, vols spatiaux habités et satellites
israel.description:
Vast is developing next-generation space stations and space infrastructure using an incremental, hardware-rich, and low-cost approach. Vast is rapidly developing its multi-module Haven Station to ensure a continuous human presence in space for America and its allies, enabling advanced microgravity research and manufacturing, and unlocking a new space economy for government, corporate, and private customers. Haven Demo’s 2025 success made Vast the only operational commercial space station company to fly and operate its own spacecraft. Next, Haven-1 is expected to become the world’s first commercial space station when it launches in 2027, followed by additional Haven modules. Additionally, the company recently announced Vast Satellite, a high-power satellite product line leveraging its space station components and the heritage of Haven Demo.

Headquartered in Long Beach, California, and with more than 1,000 employees and over a billion dollars in private capital, Vast has built the facilities required to manufacture and operate America’s next space station. The company plans to develop future habitats and systems for the Moon and Mars, dedicated space stations for government partners, and other crewed systems that will unlock the expanding long-term space economy.

Vast recherche un(e) Chef de projet – Vols spatiaux habités et satellites, rattaché(e) au Directeur des programmes européens et des ventes.

Ce poste consiste à piloter les activités de prospection, de réponse aux appels d’offres, de déploiement des campagnes commerciales et de suivi des programmes européens liés aux vols spatiaux habités et aux systèmes satellitaires.

En étroite collaboration avec les équipes de développement commercial, d’ingénierie et de gestion de mission du siège de Vast, le/la titulaire du poste assurera l’interface technique et programmatique entre les clients et partenaires européens et le site de Long Beach, en Californie.

Vast Europe est une équipe à taille humaine travaillant en étroite collaboration avec ses clients : agences spatiales, gouvernements, grands groupes industriels et clients privés à travers l’Europe. Le/la candidat(e) idéal(e) sera amené(e) à jongler entre la gestion des propositions, l’exécution des programmes, la coordination technique avec le siège et les échanges directs avec les clients, parfois au cours d’une même semaine.

Cette polyvalence est pleinement assumée, et nous recherchons une personne qui y voit un atout plutôt qu’une contrainte. Ce poste implique une collaboration étroite avec les équipes d’ingénierie, de gestion de mission, juridiques et financières du siège.

Il s’agit d’un poste à temps plein, en CDI, basé dans notre bureau de Paris, siège européen de Vast. Rémunération selon profil et expérience.

Principales responsabilités

- Piloter la préparation et la gestion des propositions, offres et réponses aux appels d’offres institutionnels  (notamment auprès de l’ESA, des agences spatiales nationales et des institutions européennes)  ainsi que des opportunités commerciales, en coordonnant les contributions des équipes d’ingénierie, de gestion de mission, juridiques et financières du siège.

- Assurer une veille active sur les programmes institutionnels européens, les cycles de financement et les opportunités d’approvisionnement pertinents pour Vast, et contribuer à la stratégie de conquête de marchés aux côtés du Directeur des programmes et des ventes européens.

- Gérer les calendriers, livrables, jalons et la coordination interne des campagnes commerciales européennes et des programmes en phase de démarrage dans les domaines des vols spatiaux habités ( notamment les missions d’astronautes privés, Haven-1 et Haven-2)  ainsi que des activités satellitaires.

- Traduire les exigences des clients en données exploitables pour les équipes d’ingénierie et de gestion de mission du siège, et restituer aux clients les contraintes techniques et programmatiques de manière claire et structurée.

- Préparer et tenir à jour les supports de présentation, descriptifs techniques et documentations de programme destinés aux interlocuteurs institutionnels et commerciaux européens.

- Soutenir les réunions clients, les échanges techniques et les négociations avec les agences, maîtres d’œuvre et clients commerciaux, en intervenant le cas échéant en qualité d’ingénieur commercial, en pleine coordination avec les équipes de développement commercial basées aux États-Unis.

- Représenter Vast lors de conférences européennes, journées sectorielles, événements organisés par les agences et autres rencontres relevant de l’écosystème spatial européen.

- Assurer, selon les délégations reçues, l’intérim du Directeur des programmes et des ventes européens sur les sujets liés aux programmes et aux appels d’offres, et contribuer à l’intégration ainsi qu’au développement des membres juniors de l’équipe.

- Apporter un soutien à l’équipe élargie de Vast Europe dans le cadre d’activités connexes, notamment en matière de relations institutionnelles et de développement de partenariats industriels, selon les priorités.

Profil requis

- Diplôme de niveau licence ou supérieur en ingénierie, sciences, discipline technique, commerce ou domaine connexe.

- Plus de 5 ans d’expérience en gestion de programmes, gestion d’appels d’offres et de soumissions, ou gestion de projets orientés client dans le secteur spatial ou aérospatial.

- Expérience directe auprès de clients institutionnels européens et bonne connaissance des processus d’achat public et d’approvisionnement, notamment auprès de l’ESA, de l’Union européenne et/ou des agences spatiales nationales.

- Expérience avérée comme interface principale entre un programme et un client externe, tant sur les aspects techniques que managériaux.

- Excellentes compétences en communication et en gestion des parties prenantes.

- Maîtrise professionnelle de l’anglais indispensable. Maitrise du francais et/ou d’autres langues européennes fortement souhaitée.

- Autorisation légale de travailler en France requise.

Compétences souhaitées

- Diplôme de niveau master ou équivalent en ingénierie, sciences, commerce ou domaine connexe.

- Maîtrise professionnelle du français ; la connaissance d’autres langues européennes constitue un atout.

- Expérience des programmes ou missions de vols spatiaux habités, incluant une bonne connaissance des fournisseurs de véhicules habités et des campagnes d’intégration au lancement.

- Expérience auprès de clients institutionnels et commerciaux.

- Solides compétences en rédaction technique et en rédaction de propositions, notamment en matière de documentation d’interfaces multipartites et de programmes complexes.

- Expérience dans un environnement de start-up ou de petite structure, avec la capacité de travailler de manière autonome lorsque nécessaire.

- Solides compétences en négociation, priorisation et coordination interfonctionnelle, avec la capacité de s’adapter rapidement à des changements de cap stratégique.

- Capacité à participer ponctuellement à des réunions en dehors des horaires habituels, afin de tenir compte des fuseaux horaires ou de soutenir des étapes critiques des missions, dans le respect de la législation applicable.

- Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills.

- Strong written communication skills in English, including briefs, summaries, and proposal inputs.

- Strong organizational skills and proficiency with spreadsheets and presentation tools for analysis and reporting.

- Eligibility to work in France.

Preferred Skills & Experience

- Master’s degree in an engineering, science, or business discipline.

- Experience with human spaceflight programs or missions, and familiarity with crewed vehicle providers and launch integration campaigns.

- Experience with a CRM (Salesforce or similar) and research or list-building tools.

- Experience spanning both institutional and commercial space customers.

israel.description:

Vast is rapidly developing its multi-module Haven Station to ensure a continuous human presence in space for America and its allies, enabling advanced microgravity research and manufacturing, and unlocking a new space economy for government, corporate, and private customers. Haven Demo’s 2025 success made Vast the only operational commercial space station company to fly and operate its own spacecraft. Next, Haven-1 is expected to become the world’s first commercial space station when it launches in 2027, followed by additional Haven modules. Additionally, the company recently announced Vast Satellite, a high-power satellite product line leveraging its space station components and the heritage of Haven Demo.

Headquartered in Long Beach, California, and with more than 1,000 employees and over a billion dollars in private capital, Vast has built the facilities required to manufacture and operate America’s next space station. The company plans to develop future habitats and systems for the Moon and Mars, dedicated space stations for government partners, and other crewed systems that will unlock the expanding long-term space economy.

Vast is looking for a Propulsion Design Reliability Engineer, reporting to the Director of Design Reliability, to guide the design, verification, and validation of Haven-1, an  the world's first commercial human-rated space station..

As a Propulsion Design Reliability Engineer, you will ensure the propulsion system on Haven-1 is appropriately designed and functions reliably, without failure, over their intended lifespan by integrating reliability principles directly into the design process. You will drive Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA), guide test plan definition and review verification & validation data, and facilitate design teams to prevent failures before manufacturing. You will work closely with hardware teams to ensure build practices meet design intent, define test methodologies, and analyze field data to improve design robustness. You will be responsible for shepherding the Haven-1 propulsion system through detailed design and transitioning the space station from design,  to a built and tested station ready to host humans in space.

This will be a full-time, exempt position located in our Long Beach location.



Responsibilities:

- Technical Leadership: Guide design of the propulsion systems for a large scale space station.

- Cultivate Vast's understanding of static and dynamic loads, vibrations, thermal, combustion and other propulsion considerations to drive design decisions.

- Lead the technical reviews providing clear, decisive guidance of mechanical design and analysis, manufacturing drawings, test plans, concept of operations, during milestone design reviews and major risk gates.

- Provide critical peer review and approval of hardware designs during design reviews, and of acceptance and qualification test campaigns

- Ensure that the Vast's design process & design criteria/requirements are being followed for flight, launch, and ground support systems.

- Set the standard for acceptance and qualification test completeness for flight systems, ensuring our test campaigns are robust, disciplined, and aligned with human-rated reliability.

- Bring deep engineering intuition to test campaigns, identifying risks early and helping teams converge on safe, resilient solutions.

- Design Excellence: Architect Vast’s propulsion engineering standards, design guides, and review frameworks; build tools that enable fast, confident decision-making at all levels across the company.

- Develop design criteria, requirements, and verification approaches to support haven-1 design architecture

- Make engineering best practices accessible and actionable, especially for engineers moving rapidly under ambitious program timelines.

- Support and elevate engineering teams across the organization by bringing broad experience in design, build cycles, integration, and test.

- Turn organizational knowledge into lasting guidance by capturing lessons learned and strengthening future standards.

- Process Ownership: Build and steward the processes that ensure engineering rigor at scale—ensuring designs meet standards, reviews are comprehensive, and changes are consistently implemented.

- Own and continuously refine design review templates, reliability checklists, and internal design guides.

- Track design maturity and compliance across the station and vehicle architecture, ensuring nothing slips through the cracks.

- Build tools, frameworks, and automation that empower engineers to explore design trade-offs and risks with clarity and speed.

- Change and Configuration management: Work across all facets of the engineering organization to improve vehicle reliability.

- Partner with configuration and change management so that every update to flight hardware is intentional, reviewed, and fully understood.

- Drive technical trades for the vehicle and enable decisions backed by strong physics based engineering rational

- Coordinate between Change Management, Risk, and Engineering teams to ensure design revisions drive continuous improvement on the vehicle

- Partner with the internal software team to ensure system data, configuration details, and design decisions are well organized and accessible.

- Risk Management: Partner with the Risk management team to identify Risk, and drive design improvements with engineering to mitigate.

- Work with Risk Management and Engineering to quantify Risk and failure probability through rigorous engineering rational

- Drive FMEA and Fault tree analysis across all engineering systems to identify and drive down risk

- Drive best practices for traceability and verification & validation of design revisions to thoroughly document risk mitigations across flight, launch, and ground support systems.

Minimum Qualifications:

- Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Physics, or related Engineering discipline

- 6+ years of related professional work experience in responsible engineering, design ownership, systems integration, test engineering, or reliability-focused development.

Preferred Skills & Experience:

- 10+ years of related professional work experience in responsible engineering, design ownership, systems integration, test engineering, or reliability-focused development.

- Experience in Responsible Engineering, Systems Engineering, Office of the Chief Engineer, or Reliability Engineering roles on complex aerospace systems.

- Hands-on experience designing, assembling, integrating, or testing hardware.

- Background with spacecraft, aircraft, launch vehicles, or other mission- or safety-critical systems.

- Familiarity with fracture control, reliability methodologies, or human-rated hardware standards.

- Experience creating engineering standards, review templates, or technical guidance frameworks.

- Strong scripting and data analysis skills (Python, MATLAB, Excel) and familiarity with visualization tools (e.g., Tableau).

- Knowledge of manufacturing processes, materials selection, and hardware qualification pathways.

- Strong systems-level intuition and the ability to anticipate and articulate risks early.

Additional Requirements:

- Willingness to work overtime, or weekends to support critical mission milestones.

$162,360—$265,392 USD

- Own tank requirements and interfaces with Propulsion, ECLSS, and Structures

- Support the responsible engineers with the liner supplier, the winder, and the metallic fabrication shops on specifications, deviations, inspection, and acceptance

- Write and defend the qualification and fracture control approach for crewed flight

- 4+ years of experience designing, analyzing, or testing pressure vessels or composite structures for flight or other high consequence use

- Composite overwrapped pressure vessel design, analysis, or test, for propulsion, life support, or any other application

- Design and qualification to AIAA S-081 or S-080

- Fracture control for crewed spacecraft per NASA-STD-5019

- Filament winding pattern design and composite manufacturing

- Titanium tank fabrication: forgings, superplastic forming, welding, heat treatment, and inspection

- Propellant management device design

- Type IV hydrogen or CNG tank development

- Analysis in Ansys, Abaqus, or Femap/Nastran, including laminate analysis. WoundSim or similar winding simulation is a plus

Vast is seeking a Senior GNC Engineer to own guidance, navigation, and control for a new constellation-ready spacecraft bus — a product line designed to scale to hundreds of spacecraft per year.

The satellite bus uses a CMG-based attitude control system — four Vast Mini CMGs in a pyramid configuration. ADCS performance is a defining capability of the bus — it's what enables high-power payloads that demand precise pointing and rapid slew. You'll own the GNC algorithms, simulation environment, sensor suite definition, and pointing performance for the satellite.

This is end-to-end ADCS ownership: from architecture trades and algorithm development through 6DOF simulation, hardware-in-the-loop testing, and on-orbit commissioning. You'll engage directly with payload customers on pointing and stability requirements, and you'll define the CMG and sensor performance specs that drive hardware development and procurement across the program.

This will be a full-time, exempt position located in our Long Beach location.

Responsibilities:

- Define the ADCS architecture — CMG pyramid configuration, sensor suite selection, pointing modes (nadir+yaw steer, LVLH fixed, 3-axis sun tracking)

- Develop GNC algorithms — attitude determination, CMG steering law (including singularity avoidance), momentum management, desaturation strategy

- Own the pointing budget — pointing accuracy, stability, jitter, and smear allocation across the sensor and actuator chain

- Define the simulation strategy — determine how the spacecraft design, simulation, and digital twin tool and Vast’s flight-validated 6DOF physics sim (GTsim) work together, what fidelity is needed for upfront system design vs flight readiness

- Build and validate the 6DOF simulation environment

- Define CMG performance requirements — momentum capacity, gimbal rate, gimbal limits, pyramid angle — feeding the electronics lead for box design

- Define sensor performance requirements — star tracker, IMU, sun sensor, magnetometer, GNSS receiver accuracy and noise specs (feeding the procurement lead for vendor selection)

- Support CMG Rev 1 bring-up with closed-loop testing

- Define and commission the HITL (hardware-in-the-loop) lab — flight processor, spoofed I/O, real-time simulation

- Magnetic field modeling for torque rod sizing

- Run Monte Carlo analysis campaigns to demonstrate pointing performance and flight readiness

- Assess flexible body dynamics — structural mode coupling with large solar arrays and cantilevered payloads, define appendage first-mode frequency requirements for structures

- Engage directly with payload customers on pointing and stability requirements — assess feasibility on the bus, define GNC data interfaces, and negotiate what we can support

- Ensure controllability during electric propulsion maneuvers — coordinate with the EP team on thrust vector, disturbance torques, and momentum impact

- Build a GNC team as the program scales — define roles and hire as complexity demands

- Support on-orbit commissioning planning for ADCS

Minimum Qualifications:

- Bachelor's degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Physics, Mathematics, or a related technical discipline

- 6+ years of spacecraft GNC or ADCS development experience

- GNC algorithm development experience for spacecraft — attitude determination, control law design, actuator management

- Experience with reaction wheels or CMGs — actuator sizing, control allocation, momentum management

- Built and validated 6DOF spacecraft simulations

- Pointing budget development and allocation across sensor/actuator chains

- HITL test environment design and execution

- Comfortable working from architecture trades through flight software implementation

- Strong dynamics and controls fundamentals

Preferred Qualifications:

- Able to obtain a security clearance

- CMG experience — steering laws, singularity avoidance, pyramid configuration optimization

- Momentum management for LEO spacecraft (magnetic desaturation, gravity gradient)

- Star tracker and IMU selection / characterization experience

- Agile / small-sat GNC development — you've done this with a small team on a fast timeline

- GNC flight software implementation experience

This will be a full-time, exempt position located in our Long Beach location.

About this role:

We're designing a high-power satellite bus that accommodates multiple payload types — including a compute-intensive Nvidia payload with significant thermal dissipation. The thermal architecture is a first-order design decision for this bus, not an afterthought. You'll own thermal analysis and design from system architecture through flight delivery, starting during the architecture trade studies.

The thermal challenges span the full range: multiple payload configurations with different thermal profiles, high-power-density electronics with demanding heat rejection requirements, and a production-rate design that must be repeatable across hundreds of spacecraft. You'll start as the sole thermal engineer and build a team as the program scales.

Responsibilities:

- Define the thermal control architecture — trade passive, heat pipe, and pumped fluid loop approaches, radiator sizing and placement

- Perform system-level and component-level thermal analysis for the satellite bus across all payload configurations

- Address the high-power thermal challenge — Nvidia compute module drives heat rejection requirements that may force the architecture

- Contribute first-order thermal models to the spacecraft design, simulation, and digital twin tool for fast design iteration, then validate using traditional analysis tools (e.g., Thermal Desktop)

- Develop and maintain the detailed system thermal model

- Own the thermal budget — min/max temperatures per component vs qualification limits, across all orbital conditions

- Select thermal coatings and materials (AZ-93, S13G, Kapton, Aeroglaze, etc.)

- Specify and procure emissivity control materials and RTDs (temperature sensors)

- Plan TVAC test campaigns — define chamber requirements, test profiles, success criteria (feeds facility planning)

- Correlate thermal models to test data after environmental testing

- Support solar array thermal analysis (coordinate with solar array team lead)

- Support box-level thermal design for new clean-sheet avionics designs — power dissipation, interface temperatures, mounting thermal resistance

Minimum Qualifications:

- Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical discipline

- 6+ years of spacecraft or aerospace thermal engineering experience

- Spacecraft thermal control design and analysis experience — passive and active systems

- Built and correlated thermal models for flight hardware

- Experience with high-power / high-dissipation thermal challenges

- Familiar with thermal coatings, MLI, radiators, heat pipes, thermal straps

- TVAC test planning and execution experience

- Comfortable working during early architecture phases — you can make thermal architecture recommendations with incomplete data and refine as the design matures

- Experience across multiple thermal analysis tools (Thermal Desktop, SINDA, ESATAN, or equivalent)

Preferred Skills & Experience:

- Able to obtain a security clearance

- Experience with multi-satellite builds where thermal design must be consistent across units

- High-power-density thermal design experience

- Thermal design for payloads with variable duty cycles

- Cryogenic or specialized thermal control experience

israel.description:
Vast is developing next-generation space stations and space infrastructure using an incremental, hardware-rich, and low-cost approach. Vast is rapidly developing its multi-module Haven Station to ensure a continuous human presence in space for America and its allies, enabling advanced microgravity research and manufacturing, and unlocking a new space economy for government, corporate, and private customers. Haven Demo’s 2025 success made Vast the only operational commercial space station company to fly and operate its own spacecraft. Next, Haven-1 is expected to become the world’s first commercial space station when it launches in 2027, followed by additional Haven modules. Additionally, the company recently announced Vast Satellite, a high-power satellite product line leveraging its space station components and the heritage of Haven Demo.

Headquartered in Long Beach, California, and with more than 1,000 employees and over a billion dollars in private capital, Vast has built the facilities required to manufacture and operate America’s next space station. The company plans to develop future habitats and systems for the Moon and Mars, dedicated space stations for government partners, and other crewed systems that will unlock the expanding long-term space economy.

Vast is looking for a Welder and Fabrication Technician II, reporting to the Production Manager of Primary Structures Fabrication, to support the development of the systems that will be required for the design and build of artificial-gravity human-rated space stations.

This will be a full-time, non-exempt position located in our Long Beach location.

Responsibilities:

- Weld the Haven Structure for Human spaceflight

- Operate mechanized and robotic welding equipment

- Ability to quickly fabricate, weld tooling to support Haven.

- Inspect fabricated parts for geometry acceptance and weld conformance

- Fit, form parts, and clean parts as required and setup welding equipment in preparation for welding

- Perform Class A quality Aluminum weld

- Diagnose weld defects and suggest corrective actions, both in repair and process optimization

- Work with Engineering to improve tools and problem solve

- Material handling of raw goods and finished weldments

- Experience with a wide variety of metal fabrication equipment such as vertical bandsaw, Sanding equipment, Capability to efficiently set up jig tables.

Minimum Qualifications:

- 2+ years of experience with Class A TIG

- 2+ years of experience with fabrication, and forming experience

Preferred Skills & Experience:

- Self-starter, highly motivated working in a fast-paced department

- Automated/robotic welding experience Preferred VPPAW

- 5+ or more years with Class A aerospace welding

- Ability to follow written and verbal instruction

- Familiar working with x-ray technicians and other NDT techniques

- Experience reading engineering blueprints

Additional Requirements:

- Ability to travel up to 10% of the time

- Willingness to work evenings and/or weekends to support critical mission milestones

israel.title: Account Executive
israel.description:
About Flexport:

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.

The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.

Own your portfolio and drive strategic growth across global trade.

The opportunity:

The Sales team at Flexport is critical to our mission, fostering deep, lasting relationships that drive client success and accelerate global trade. As an Account Executive II (Farmer), you operate with independence. You own a portfolio of accounts and are the architect of their success — not just the executor of a plan. Your clients are growing in complexity: multiple trade lanes, operational nuance, and real expansion potential. You know Flexport's product suite well enough to connect client needs to solutions with confidence, and you drive revenue growth within your book without being directed. Senior leadership trusts your judgment on the accounts you own. This is where you move from learning the craft to mastering it.

- You will:

- Own the success and retention of a portfolio of Flexport clients, managing relationships independently and proactively — you identify problems before clients raise them.

- Lead all client communications and strategic engagements, including QBRs/MBRs, without requiring support from senior teammates for routine situations.

- Identify and execute cross-sell and upsell opportunities within your book of business, owning the commercial outcome end-to-end.

- Collaborate cross-functionally with Operations, Product, Sales, and Implementation to solve client problems with urgency and creativity.

- Analyze client performance data to spot trends, anticipate risks, and bring data-backed recommendations to every client conversation.

- Develop a clear point of view on each client's business — not just their Flexport usage, but their supply chain strategy and where Flexport fits.

- Work closely with Hunters from the beginning of the customer journey to ensure a seamless transition and long-term client success.

You should have:

- 3+ years of experience in account management, direct sales, client success, or a similar client-facing role; logistics, supply chain, or SaaS background preferred.

- Proven ability to independently manage a portfolio of accounts, with measurable retention and expansion results.

- A demonstrated track record of identifying and closing cross-sell/upsell opportunities — you move deals forward without being pushed.

- Strong communication and presentation skills; comfortable leading senior stakeholder conversations without support.

- Data literacy: you pull insights from client metrics and use them to drive conversations and decisions.

- A 'compliance first' attitude to keep our regulators happy and enthusiastic about Flexport since we operate in a heavily regulated industry.

You will get:

- Real ownership — your book of business is yours to win, grow, and protect.

- A seat at the table on cross-functional client strategy work with Sales, Product, and Operations.

- Access to a growing product suite and the training to position it effectively.

- Competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and a hybrid work environment.

You don't just manage these relationships; you shape them. You bring a strategic point of view to every client engagement, lead business reviews that drive meaningful decisions, and connect the dots across Flexport's full product suite to unlock growth. You operate with full autonomy, deliver against a high bar on revenue and retention, and are increasingly the person junior teammates turn to when they need guidance.

- Lead RFP bids and renewals end-to-end

- Serve as a true strategic partner to clients, going deep on their supply chain operations to identify where Flexport can unlock efficiency, reduce cost, or introduce new capabilities.

- Lead high-impact business reviews (QBRs/MBRs) that go beyond reporting — you bring market context, multi-modal insights, and tailored recommendations that shift how clients think about their supply chain.

- Drive cross-sell and upsell across Flexport's full product suite, consistently meeting or exceeding revenue and retention targets.

- Strong commercial instincts: you see growth opportunities before clients ask for them and you close them.

Account Executive, Flexport Capital

Flexport helps more than 10,000 clients and suppliers lead all aspects of their supply chain operations. Each of these customers faces significant working capital burdens that hamper their ability to grow their businesses. Since inception, Flexport Capital has provided over $2 billion in loans to Flexport customers to address these needs. Our non-dilutive capital products empower businesses to grow and bridge their working capital needs while maintaining ownership and control. As a start-up within a start-up, we’re developing unique fintech products that leverage the resources and data of Flexport’s platform for global trade. We are seeking an entrepreneurial and financially savvy individual to join our tight-knit team.

The Opportunity: Flexport Capital is Flexport’s financing arm, offering inventory and logistics financing, asset-based lending, term loans, and working capital products to Flexport clients. As an Account Executive, you will own the full end-to-end sales cycle for Flexport Capital, from sourcing, prospecting, negotiation, underwriting coordination, and close. You will build and manage your own growing book of business. You will serve as the primary commercial voice for your customers, acting as a financial consultant and strategic advisor to founders, CFOs, and finance teams seeking working capital solutions. You will work directly with Credit, Product, and Legal as a peer partner, shaping product development and go-to-market strategy based on real market feedback. You’ll play a critical role in scaling Flexport Capital’s market presence and establishing it as the go-to financing partner for growth stage businesses. You’ll own building the sales playbook that drives this growth, with full autonomy over your territory and clear upside as you scale.

You Will:

- Own the full end-to-end sales cycle for your territory, from sourcing and prospecting through deal structuring, underwriting coordination, closing, and early relationship management.

- Build and own a growing book of business with direct revenue accountability. You'll win new customers, expand relationships as they scale, and identify cross-sell opportunities within your territory.

- Serve as the commercial relationship owner for your clients. You'll negotiate terms, structure deals, and coordinate with Credit through underwriting to close.

- Use Flexport's supply chain data as a commercial advantage. By analyzing shipment patterns, volume spikes, transit times, and invoice data, you can identify when customers need capital and turn those signals into targeted actions to drive sustainable growth.

- Drive strategic initiatives related to growth strategy, sales motions, and capital markets partnerships that expand Flexport Capital's market position.

- Leverage Flexport's freight and omni capabilities to create working capital solutions that deepen customer relationships, increase wallet share, and win deals competitors can't.

You Should Have:

- Experience - 6+ years of experience in sales/sales development for a financial services and/or a technology company. Previous startup experience is a plus.

- Financial & Credit Acumen - Fluency in working capital structures, financial statement analysis, and lending mechanics. You can read and interpret P&Ls, balance sheets, and cash flow statements to assess customer needs. You'll be expected to recommend appropriate lending structures and create tailored working capital solutions for each prospect based on their business model and financing needs.

- Full-cycle sales execution - You’ve owned deals from prospect through close. You understand pipeline management, deal structuring, and how to navigate complex sales cycles. You’ve hit and exceeded quota consistently.

- Communication & Presence - Excellent communication and executive presence. You can build trusted relationships with Founders, CEOs, CFOs, and Finance Directors. You navigate senior-level conversations with ease and represent your company credibly with C-suite buyers.

- Commercial drive and ownership - You’re motivated by building and growing a business. You think like an owner, take accountability for outcomes, and proactively solve problems to move deals forward.

- Strategic business sense - You see beyond individual deals. You understand market trends, competitive threats, and identify customer needs that create product/GTM opportunities.

- Data & Tools - Proficiency in Salesforce, Excel, Claude, and other data tools. Ability to design dashboards and reporting frameworks to track pipeline growth and buying signals.

The Opportunity

We’re looking for an Accounts Receivable Collections Analyst who wants to use AI and agents to help customers pay on time. You’ll manage a portfolio of customer accounts, using AI to prioritize outreach, investigate overdue balances, and move payment issues toward resolution. You’ll combine these tools with clear communication and strong relationships with customers’ Accounts Payable teams.

This role is open to people starting their careers or moving into finance. Curiosity, persistence, and good judgment matter more than a traditional collections background. You’ll help shape how our team works with AI, learning our accounts receivable processes as you go. The role reports to the Head of North American Collections.

You Will

- Use AI tools and agents to prioritize assigned accounts, draft personalized email follow-ups, and track payment commitments. Pair these workflows with phone outreach and customer conversations to help meet cash collection and days sales outstanding (DSO) targets.

- Use AI to review account aging and summarize collection activity. Check the results and keep records of customer conversations, payment promises, disputes, and next steps accurate and up to date.

- Build relationships with customers’ Accounts Payable teams and act as their point of contact for collections and payment questions.

- Coordinate incoming requests and handle initial escalations. Resolve issues promptly and bring in the right team when a problem needs further review.

- Investigate account balances with support from AI tools and teammates. Check the underlying invoices and payment history, recommend next steps, and ask for help when an issue needs deeper review.

- Research invoice and payment discrepancies, reconcile account information, and work with the appropriate teams to resolve customers’ AR/AP questions.

- Work with Credit to arrange and monitor approved payment schedules for overdue accounts.

- Prepare clear account summaries with AI support and participate in biweekly reviews with business leaders on open receivables, collection risks, and next steps.

柔軟性があり、週末の勤務にもオープンな候補者を探しています。

What You'll Gain / 得られるもの

業界における先進的なシステム利用による航空貨物オペレーション（輸入、輸出、インターモーダル）における深い専門知識。

Na Flexport, acreditamos que o comércio global pode impulsionar o progresso da humanidade. Por isso, nossa missão é make global commerce so easy there will be more of its.

Estamos moldando o futuro de uma indústria de US$ 10 trilhões com soluções impulsionadas por tecnologia inovadora e pessoas excepcionais. Hoje, empresas de todos os tamanhos — desde marcas emergentes até empresas da Fortune 500 — utilizam a tecnologia da Flexport para movimentar mais de US$ 19 bilhões em mercadorias por ano, em 112 países.

A recente crise global da cadeia de suprimentos colocou a Flexport no centro das atenções, enquanto continuamos desempenhando um papel fundamental na forma como as mercadorias são movimentadas ao redor do mundo. Temos orgulho de contar com o apoio dos melhores investidores do mercado, que acreditam em nossa missão, em nossas soluções e em nossas pessoas.

Pronto para enfrentar desafios globais que impactam os negócios, a sociedade e o meio ambiente? Venha fazer parte do nosso time.

A oportunidade:

À medida que a Flexport continua expandindo suas operações pela América Latina, em São Paulo se encontra o primeiro escritório da Flexport no Brasil. Você estará entre os primeiros profissionais contratados localmente, fazendo parte do time inicial responsável por construir essa operação desde o início.

Como Operations Associate, você terá um papel fundamental na missão da Flexport de tornar o comércio global mais simples e eficiente, contribuindo para que ele continue crescendo. Hoje, a Flexport movimenta mais de US$ 175 bilhões em mercadorias para mais de 13.000 clientes em 135 países. Nesta vaga, seu foco será ajudar a desenvolver essa operação no Brasil, trabalhando de forma próxima e integrada com clientes, parceiros locais, armadores, companhias aéreas, terminais portuários e aeroportuários, transportadoras, despachantes aduaneiros e equipes da Flexport em diferentes partes do mundo.

Essa vaga é ideal para alguém que queira transformar a operação logística no Brasil por meio de automação e inteligência artificial, em vez de simplesmente administrar os processos existentes. A Flexport está investindo fortemente na automação de atividades operacionais manuais em toda a América Latina e você terá um papel importante em trazer essas soluções para a realidade da operação em São Paulo.

Suas responsabilidades

- Supervisionar a coordenação dos embarques de importação e exportação nos modais marítimo, aéreo e rodoviário, realizados pelo agente da Flexport no Brasil, garantindo níveis de serviço, conformidade e eficiência em todas as etapas do processo

- Atuar como ponto focal para temas relacionados ao Brasil, trabalhando em conjunto com equipes locais, regionais e globais, incluindo Sales, Account Management, Trade Lane Managers e Operations, no desenvolvimento de soluções logísticas, resolução de problemas, identificação de oportunidades de melhoria e suporte à conquista e expansão de novos negócios para a Flexport

- Atuar como ponto focal para clientes locais no Brasil, oferecendo suporte operacional sempre que necessário.

- Inglês e português fluentes são obrigatórios; espanhol será considerado um diferencial.

- Mais de 2 anos de experiência em agenciamento de cargas, co-loaders ou armadores
