israel.title: Senior Applied AI Engineer, Autonomous Supply Chains
israel.description:
About Flexport:

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.

The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.

Senior Applied AI Engineer, Autonomous Supply Chains

About Flexport

Look around you. Almost everything in the room crossed an ocean to get there. Moving one container from a factory to a warehouse takes 10 to 15 companies: truckers, customs brokers, port terminals, ocean carriers, insurers, lenders and warehouses, each with its own systems, paperwork and rules. A freight forwarder runs that whole journey, so the brand that makes the goods doesn't have to.

Most forwarders still run it on email, spreadsheets and phone calls. We call it email freight forwarding. Flexport runs it on one platform, where AI agents do the routine work and experts step in where judgment matters. We've moved $175B of goods for more than 13,000 brands across 135 countries. Our agents handle 21 million tasks a year, and up to 80% of customs work is automated.

Global logistics is a $13 trillion industry, and even the largest forwarder earns less than 3% of global logistics outsourcing revenue. People-powered operations don't scale: to grow, you hire. Software broke that ceiling for taxis with Uber, and for payments with Adyen and Stripe. Freight is next.

Amsterdam is one of Flexport's six engineering hubs, alongside San Francisco, Seattle, Chicago, Shanghai and Shenzhen. We own four domains end to end: Customs Technology, Autonomous Supply Chains (Applied AI), Platform and Security. See what we build at amsterdam-engineering.flexport.com.

The team: Autonomous Supply Chains

Logistics is famously hard to automate, because the happy path rarely happens. One customer won't take deliveries on a Tuesday. Another wants invoices only on Fridays, with some lines merged and others renamed. Until recently, people handled all of that by hand. Now operators use Forge, the agentic platform we build, to automate their own work: catching anomalies, routing exceptions, escalating stuck containers and adjusting invoices to each customer. Forge remembers every customer's rules and learns from every workflow run, so it gets smarter every day.

Autonomous Supply Chains is our Applied AI team: small, senior and reporting to the VP of Engineering. Self-driving cars are rated from level 0 to level 5. Most of the freight industry still runs at level 0: people emailing spreadsheets. Our goal is level 5 for freight, with Forge as the best agentic platform there is, handling every complexity, every calamity and every odd preference without skipping a beat.

Stack: TypeScript, Rust, Next.js, Temporal, Postgres and Snowflake, with models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Google.

The role

As a Senior Applied AI Engineer on Autonomous Supply Chains, you'll build the agents and AI-powered applications that make Flexport's operations faster and increasingly autonomous. You'll find the most painful problems in our operations, design the solution and ship it to operators moving freight across 135 countries. This isn't a role where you join a team and pick up tickets.

What you'll do

- Design and ship end-to-end AI agents that handle real logistics work, such as customs compliance, document processing, invoice validation and exception management.

- Build the evaluation, guardrails and human-in-the-loop flows that make an agent trustworthy enough to run 24/7.

- Stay on top of what's happening in the world of AI, and channel those innovations straight into the product. When Jev came out this fall, we had three use cases live within two weeks.

- Work directly with operators, domain experts and leadership to turn ambiguous problems into shipped products, and measure whether they worked.

- Move fast from idea to production, and treat every deployment as a chance to learn.

- Cross organizational boundaries to understand problems deeply and get things done without waiting for permission.

You should have

- 5+ years of software engineering experience, and you've built seriously with LLMs, whether in production, in side projects or just because you couldn't stop yourself.

- LLM fluency: agent patterns, tool use, RAG, prompt design and evaluation. You know the difference between what works in production and what looks good in a demo.

- Full-stack capability in TypeScript and Next.js. You can own a feature end to end.

- Product instinct: you can tell what's worth building, not just how to build it.

- Clear written and spoken communication in English, including design docs that people actually read.

Nice to have

- Experience with workflow orchestration, such as Temporal.

- Experience building internal tools or operator-facing applications.

How we work

- We value builders. People who think end to end, do their own discovery and ship independently. Nobody hands you a spec.

- Your users sit next to you. Operators, customs experts and account teams work in the same office. Watch them use your tool, and fix it before dessert.

- Any model, any harness. Use any frontier model from Anthropic, OpenAI or Google, in all the popular coding harnesses. Our engineers manage swarms of coding agents from their first week.

- We ship dozens of times a day, with continuous deployment and a platform team obsessed with making it safe and fast.

- Hybrid, in English. We're together in our office on Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal, a few minutes from Dam Square, three days a week*. The other days are flexible. English is our working language, and we work daily with colleagues in the US and China.

- No logistics background needed. Almost nobody joins knowing what an HTS code or a bill of lading is. The experts sit a few desks away.

- Agile, but not dogmatic. Teams decide how they work best.

Why this role is special

- Your work is visible: a small, senior team that reports to the VP of Engineering. What you build gets noticed, and your ideas shape the direction.

- Real stakes: your agents act on real shipments for 13,000+ brands in 135 countries, so the impact is immediate and measurable.

- You're early: the playbook for applied AI in logistics hasn't been written yet. You'll help write it.

What's in it for you

- Equity for everyone: every team member becomes a shareholder in a pre-IPO company in a multi-trillion dollar industry.

- 25 vacation days, based on full-time employment, plus Dutch public holidays.

- Health insurance, fully paid: a collective plan with basic and additional packages. Flexport pays the monthly premium.

- Pension: a defined contribution scheme.

- Breakfast and lunch: daily catered lunch with vegetarian options, breakfast, snacks and drinks in the office.

- Commute covered: Flexport covers home-to-office commuting costs if you live outside Amsterdam.

- Parental leave: time off for both parents to bond with a new child.

- Wellbeing support: an Employee Assistance Program through Aetna for you and your household, at no cost.

- Visa sponsorship: we sponsor visas for the right candidates and help you move to Amsterdam. Eligible international hires may also benefit from the Dutch expat tax ruling.

Our hiring process

- Application review: our team reviews your application.

- Recruiter screen: talk about your experience, the role and your questions about Flexport.

- Remote coding: your first coding interview takes place over video.

- Onsite coding and system design: a second coding interview and system design in our office.

- Project deep dive: discuss a project from your experience with the hiring manager.

- Team debrief: the interview team reviews feedback together. You don't attend this step.

- Offer: if there's a match, your recruiter walks you through the offer.

An additional remote coding round may be needed if the earlier coding interviews leave questions to resolve. Your recruiter will confirm the plan before interviews begin. We only contact candidates from @flexport.com addresses, and we will never ask you for money or banking details.

Our business, product, and engineering teams collaborate closely with our Data Scientists to share domain knowledge, test hypotheses at scale, and develop promising solutions that can be quickly and widely deployed. Our ideal candidate is: self-motivated, technically excellent at writing code, and passionate about delivering cutting-edge solutions.

You should have:

- A degree in a quantitative field like Operations Research, Applied Mathematics, Computer Science, Econometrics, etc.

- 5+ years of industry experience in solving optimization and/or machine learning problems and developing practically efficient, automated solutions

- Experience developing, enhancing, and maintaining end-to-end data science production processes, including data modeling, algorithm development, testing, and metric tracking

- Software engineering experience to build software to solve real industrial problems, with a strong understanding of system architecture

Working knowledge of large language models and emerging interoperability standards such as Model Context Protocol. You’ll join a team operating with the agility of a startup and the data advantage of a global logistics leader. This is a hands-on environment for builders, not observers. Flexport today connects almost 10,000 clients and suppliers across 109 countries. Your work directly supports Flexport’s end customers in achieving their logistics goals. Most importantly, you will play a pivotal role in building the next operational model at Flexport: allowing us to effectively scale to achieve our mission of making global trade easier for everyone.

This role is designed to facilitate the movement of shipments while discovering and driving efficiencies that build and improve operations as part of our Global team. You will be responsible for ensuring that all customer shipments are executed according to plan, on time and within budget. As the person who manages movement in your region with laser focus, you have the unique opportunity to help your regional account team spot opportunities to improve and grow our customers’ business. You will drive impact through surfacing new ideas to eliminate waste, improve customer experience or introducing innovative ways of managing a supply chain.

Responsibilities:

- Be the “front line” in ensuring the highest standard of Flexport quality: shipments move on-time and exceptions are handled appropriately

- Be responsible for ensuring your work satisfies internal KPIs and SLAs that demonstrate quality delivery

- Follow standard operating procedures (SOP)

- Solve client issues quickly and ensure smooth operations at origin and destination and escalate issues as needed

- Acting in the best interest of the company by avoiding leakages and ensuring cost conscious behavior

- Seamlessly coordinate day-to-day logistics operations with internal and external partners such as steamship lines, air carriers, intermodal and drayage vendors, customs, trade lane management, warehousing, transloading, trucking, and the air operations team

- Execute the end-to-end movement of freight shipments within a regional network (both imports and exports), including intermodal movements

- Assist the shipments managed by partners as we drive partner autonomy (if applicable in a given region)

Prerequisites:

- BA/BS Degree or completed professional training as forwarding agent

- 3+ years of experience in freight forwarding, and direct Air export experience

- Fluent in French and English (other European languages are a plus)

- Able to adapt to new technology and can thrive in a fast paced environment

- Effective time management, be able to properly prioritize and manage a large volume of tasks

- Attention to detail

- Ability to effectively seek and receive feedback

- Effective communication both verbally and in writing

- Teamwork and relationship building

- Orientation towards working smarter and adopting best practices and standardization

- Problem-solving capabilities

- A “compliance first” attitude to keep our regulators happy and enthusiastic about Flexport since we operate in a heavily regulated industry

What else:

- You will work in a beautiful office in the city center of Paris with modern office equipment and a first class connection to the public transport system of Paris.

- You will work in a fast growing and changing environment with a high motivated team, which is always open to hear your ideas

- We invest in your personal and professional development by offering you internal and external trainings

- During regular team events you can have a lot of fun with your teammates and connect with them aside from your working day

What we offer:

- An opportunity to contribute to one of the fastest-growing companies, where you’ll have the chance to create a global impact while being a part of a  thriving multinational environment

- 25 working days working days of paid annual leave per complete year of service

- The employee shall be affiliated to the French social security system (Sécurité sociale) and the mandatory supplementary pension schemes (retraite complémentaire AGIRC-ARRCO) in accordance with applicable law. Employer and employee contributions shall be calculated and deducted in accordance with statutory rates.

- 50% reimbursement of the cost of the public transportation subscription(s) used for travel between your place of residence and the workplace.

- Employer's collective supplementary health insurance scheme (mutuelle d'entreprise) as required by law. Flexport shall contribute at least 50% of the premium for the base coverage.

- Lunches compensation: EUR 12 for every day worked in the office

- Parental leave benefit: Flexport is here to support you and your families in one of the most important times in life – the birth of a child! Our parental leave program allows both mothers and partners to take time off from work for pregnancy, childbirth, and to bond with your new child.

- Equity program: every team member becomes a shareholder, aligning our success with yours. As a private company in a multi-trillion dollar industry, you have a direct stake in our collective growth and success.

israel.description:
About Flexport:

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.

Senior Manager, Financial Operations, APAC

Location: Hong Kong

About Flexport

Flexport’s mission is to make global trade so easy there will be more of it. We bring together logistics expertise, technology, and AI to help businesses manage global trade.

The Opportunity

Lead how money moves through Flexport’s Asia-Pacific (APAC) business. Based in Hong Kong, you’ll own regional accounts receivable (AR), accounts payable (AP), and freight audit, with responsibility for cash collection, payment accuracy, and the teams delivering those results.

You’ll shape how these functions operate as Flexport grows across the region. That means redesigning workflows around AI and agents, developing your team’s capabilities, and turning improvements into measurable business results. You’ll work with global finance leadership and regional partners to set priorities, resolve complex issues, and build processes that work across countries, currencies, and entities.

We’re looking for a finance leader who combines operational depth with curiosity and the ability to build. You’re comfortable challenging an established process, testing a better approach yourself, and leading a team through the change.

You Will

- Own APAC performance across AR, AP, and freight audit. Set priorities and targets, review results with global finance leadership, and take action on collection risk, payment issues, and operational backlogs.

- Improve cash collection and reduce overdue receivables. Lead collections strategy, cash application, and dispute resolution; partner with Credit, Billing, Sales, and Operations to address credit blocks and fix recurring causes of delayed payment.

- Lead accurate, timely supplier and carrier payments. Oversee invoice validation, freight charge reviews, reconciliations, and payment exceptions, resolving discrepancies with vendors and operational teams before they become recurring problems.

- Build, test, and deploy AI agents and automated workflows with Finance Systems and technical partners. Focus on practical uses such as prioritizing collections, coordinating follow-ups, reviewing invoices, matching payments, and identifying exceptions.

- Own improvements from problem definition through adoption. Set a baseline, prioritize the highest-value opportunities, test workflows against real cases, and measure their effect on accuracy, processing time, and cash performance.

- Lead and develop regional teams. Set clear expectations, coach performance, build future leaders, and help people use AI effectively while applying judgment to complex customer and vendor situations.

- Maintain strong financial controls as workflows change. Define approval and exception handling, verify automated outputs, and protect data integrity. Partner with Accounting and Tax to meet local invoicing, tax, and statutory requirements.

- Standardize processes across APAC while accounting for local requirements. Lead system testing and adoption, document operating practices, and give senior stakeholders clear recommendations on risks and investment priorities.

Success in Your First Year

- Collections improve against agreed targets, with lower overdue balances and days sales outstanding (DSO), faster dispute resolution, and fewer unresolved cash application issues.

- Supplier and carrier payments become more reliable, with better invoice accuracy, shorter processing times, and fewer aged exceptions.

- Teams use AI agents and automation in daily operations, with measured reductions in manual work and controls that remain effective.

- Regional teams have clear ownership, stronger capabilities, and consistent performance reporting that helps leadership act early.

You Should Have

- 8+ years of experience in financial operations, accounts receivable, accounts payable, or a related finance function, including 3+ years leading and developing teams in a complex or global organization.

- Deep expertise in AR or AP, with practical working knowledge across collections, payments, reconciliations, and financial controls. You can demonstrate measurable improvements in cash collection, payment performance, or operational accuracy.

- Experience managing high-volume operations across multiple entities and currencies, including APAC markets. You understand how regional payment practices, invoicing rules, and tax requirements affect day-to-day execution.

- Hands-on experience using AI and automation to improve finance work. You can explain a workflow you built or improved, how you checked its results, and what changed for the business.

- Experience leading change across functions, from defining requirements and testing systems to training teams and sustaining adoption. You can influence senior stakeholders and handle difficult customer or vendor conversations.

- Strong analytical skills and experience with enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, spreadsheets, and reporting tools. You can investigate underlying transactions, turn data into a clear recommendation, and defend the result.

- A sound grounding in accounting, internal controls, and compliance, supported by a degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field, or an equivalent professional qualification.

Helpful, but Not Required

- Experience in logistics, freight, supply chain, or freight audit; familiarity with carrier billing and payment flows.

- A professional accounting designation, experience scaling shared services, or additional languages used across APAC.

israel.description:
About Flexport:

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.

Protecting Flexport's global operations and assets, enabling secure trade worldwide.

The opportunity:

Join Flexport's dynamic Compliance Program as the Senior Manager, Supply Chain Protection & Loss Intelligence. This critical role serves as the single point of accountability for both supply chain protection and loss prevention across Flexport's entire footprint — offices, fulfillment centers, and partner sites worldwide. The Manager will be responsible for protecting Flexport employees, visitors, assets, and facilities through the design and execution of security programs, while simultaneously driving a proactive loss prevention strategy across the Omni fulfillment network.

Day-to-day, this means managing a team of 50+ contracted security officers across multiple locations, overseeing electronic security infrastructure (CCTV, access control), conducting investigations, and managing the security ticketing system. Strategically, it means building the analytical foundation to identify loss trends and security gaps before they become incidents, authoring the policies and SOPs that standardize how Flexport protects its people and assets globally, and ensuring every new facility launches with security infrastructure and protocols in place from day one.

You will partner closely with operations, facilities, and leadership to design, implement, and scale security programs for existing and future locations, ensuring our people, assets, and reputation are safeguarded as Flexport rapidly expands into new markets. This is a unique opportunity to build a unified security strategy, moving beyond reactive incident management to a data-driven, proactive approach.

You will:

- Develop and maintain security and loss prevention metrics, KPIs, and dashboards to measure program effectiveness across all facilities and regions

- Analyze incident data to identify trends, loss patterns, root causes, and emerging risks — translating findings into actionable recommendations for leadership

- Build reporting frameworks that support data-driven resource allocation, vendor performance evaluation, and security investment decisions

- Provide regular analytical reports to senior management on security posture, loss prevention outcomes, and program ROI

- Author, maintain, and enforce global security and loss prevention policies, ensuring consistency across all Flexport locations and compliance with local regulatory requirements in each jurisdiction

- Develop and implement SOPs for key security scenarios (Active Shooter, Emergency Response, High Value Cage procedures, Product Disposal, etc.)

- Create site-level security plans for new and existing facilities, tailored to local risk profiles and operational requirements

- Design and deliver training programs across physical security and loss prevention topics (emergency response, office security, travel security, incident reporting, etc.)

- Develop audit frameworks and LP checklists for site leads to execute on a recurring basis

- Manage physical security programs across all Flexport facilities globally (offices, warehouses, and partner sites), including new locations as Flexport and the Omni fulfillment network expand into new markets

- Lead security planning and infrastructure stand-up for new facilities and market entries, including site assessments, vendor selection, and system deployment

- Administer and maintain electronic security systems, including CCTV surveillance and access control platforms, and evaluate new technology deployments

- Serve as the crisis management coordinator, providing real-time threat assessments and coordinating emergency response across regions

- Coordinate with HSE, HR, Legal, and Compliance on cross-functional security and safety matters

- Drive loss prevention strategy and investigations for the Omni fulfillment network, including cargo theft, employee theft, unauthorized sellers, workplace violence, and empty package findings

- Manage the security and loss prevention ticketing syste, including triaging, updating, and resolving tickets with accurate documentation

- Identify root causes of supply chain losses and develop recommendations to reduce future risk

- Review, collect, and preserve CCTV evidence to support investigations and legal proceedings

- Manage third-party guard services across all locations, including oversight of 50+ security officers, performance tracking, and operational discipline

- Manage relationships with security integrators and onboard new vendors as required for geographic expansion

Serving as a key pillar of regional leadership, this role bridges global air freight strategy with local operational execution. You will act as a collaborative partner across cross-functional organizations (including Sales, Account Management, Global Procurement, Operations, Tech, and Finance) to expand market share, build strategic airline partnerships, and ensure flawless customer experience.

- P&L & Financial Accountability: Own full financial performance (including Tonnage/Volume, Net Revenue, and Contribution Profit, e.g. Net Revenue minus Direct Costs) for assigned regional origin/destination combinations and trade lanes.

- Performance Governance & Metrics: Co-define annual budgets with General Management and actively participate in weekly business reviews (WBRs) to report on key metrics, yield performance, target adherence, and shortfall mitigation plans.

- Continuous Process Improvement: Drive operational efficiency and take-rate expansion by identifying structural bottlenecks, grounding decisions in rigorous data analysis, and driving initiatives to "build a better machine."

2. Capacity Procurement, Pricing & Solution Design

We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.

The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.

Hundreds of engineers and thousands of freight operators around the world rely on Flexport's internal systems every single day to keep billions of dollars of freight moving. Keeping those systems — and the people who use them — secure is not a compliance checkbox. It's the core infrastructure for a company operating across 112 countries.

The PSI (Platform, Security & Infrastructure) team is looking for a Senior Security Engineer to own the security of Flexport's corporate environment: endpoints, identity systems, internal networks, and the SaaS estate. This is a security engineering role, not an IT support role, and not a role where you write policies and hope for the best. You'll build, automate, and be on the ground when things get real.

What You'll Do

Endpoint & SaaS security

- Own and mature our endpoint security stack (EDR) across macOS and Windows fleets, writing device policy as code — configuration profiles, remediation scripts, and enforcement rules — with staged rollout and rollback built in.

- Own security configuration and monitoring for Flexport's critical SaaS applications (Google Workspace, Slack, and similar) through SSPM tooling, catching risky OAuth grants and configuration drift before they become incidents.

Access management

- Drive Flexport's identity posture: SSO coverage, phishing-resistant MFA and passkey rollout, SCIM lifecycle automation, and least-privilege access across the SaaS and cloud estate.

- Lead Flexport's zero-trust journey — making sure the right people have the right access, with the right controls, verified continuously.

Detection & response

- Build and tune detection rules in our SIEM, turning signal into actionable alerts, not noise.

- Lead incident response for security events: triage, contain, remediate, and write the retrospective.

Vulnerability & risk management

- Run regular assessments of corporate endpoints and prioritize findings by real business risk.

- Manage vendor and third-party security reviews, working with procurement and legal to evaluate risk before it lands in our environment.

Security enablement & leadership

- Partner with IT, Engineering, and People teams to embed security into the way we work without creating friction that drives people to workarounds.

- Develop and maintain runbooks, playbooks, and internal documentation that make the whole team more capable, and mentor engineers earlier in their career.

- Bring a point of view on how agentic AI tools and browser-based AI assistants change what corporate security needs to watch for.

You Should Have

- Typically 5–8 years of experience in enterprise security, corporate IT security, or information security engineering — we care more about what you've built than the exact number. If you meet most of this, apply.

- Strong working knowledge of endpoint security tooling: DLP (Cyberhaven, Purview, Varonis, or similar) and EDR (CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, or similar).

- Practical SIEM experience, writing detection logic, triaging alerts, and reducing false positive noise.

- Experience leading or playing a significant role in security incident response.

- Working knowledge of cloud environments (AWS, GCP, or Azure).

Nice to Have

- Experience with network security in a cloud-first environment (ZTNA, SASE, DNS filtering).

- Hands-on experience with infrastructure-as-code tools (Terraform) for security configuration management.

- Familiarity with SCIM, OIDC, and fine-grained authorization at scale.

- Experience working in a high-growth, global technology company.

- Scripting skills in Python, Bash, or similar, for automating detection, response, and operational tasks.

- Exposure to privacy regulations relevant to a European and global context (GDPR, etc.).

How We Work

- We come to the office 3 times a week to hang out, whiteboard, and ship together.

- We have the latest hardware and software, including frontier AI models on day one.

- We're agile, but not dogmatic. Teams decide how they work best.

Why This Role Is Special

- Broad ownership: you're not a cog in a large security org — you own the corporate security posture end to end, from endpoints to observability to incident response.

- Real stakes: Flexport operates in 112 countries with a global workforce. Security here matters at a genuine scale.

- Build, don't just operate: we want to automate and engineer our way to a stronger posture, not just run playbooks.

- You're part of PSI: the platform, security, and infrastructure teams work hand in hand at Flexport. We value engineering quality and treat security as infrastructure, not just policy.

- We sponsor visas for the right candidate.

What's in it for you

- An opportunity to contribute to one of the fastest-growing companies, where you'll have the chance to create a global impact while being part of a thriving multinational environment.

- Daily catered lunches incl. vegetarian options, breakfast, snacks and soft drinks available in our office on a daily basis.

- Commute expenses: Flexport will cover home-office commuting costs for employees living outside of Amsterdam.

- 25 working days as vacation days based on full-time employment.

- Health insurance: Flexport offers a collective health insurance plan including a basic package and any available additional packages. Your monthly premium is fully paid by Flexport.

- A defined pension contribution scheme.

- Equity program: every team member becomes a shareholder, aligning our success with yours. As a private company in a multi-trillion dollar industry, you have a direct stake in our collective growth and success.

- Employee Assistance Program through Aetna Resources for Living: Flexport provides an employer-sponsored program at no cost to you and your household members.

- Parental leave benefit: Flexport is here to support you and your family during one of the most important times in life — the birth of a child. Our parental leave program allows both mothers and partners to take time off from work for pregnancy, childbirth, and to bond with your new child.

Exceptional software development is integral in allowing us to fulfill our mission of fixing the user experience in global trade. At Flexport you’ll develop products that are at the forefront of reshaping the entire logistics & supply chain industries. You’ll work alongside self-starters interested in solving real-world problems and streamlining the inefficiencies in the complex global trade industry. You’ll have the opportunity to reshape an industry by creating the new operating system for global trade.

Our engineers are top-notch software developers who love listening to the users, working as a team, and proactively taking the lead whenever necessary. The role involves learning the business of freight forwarding, modeling the work that people do to move freight, designing solutions to make it more efficient, and thinking innovatively to automate much of it. As a full stack Senior Software Engineer, you will be responsible for architecting, designing, developing, testing and maintaining critical forwarding related systems. In addition, as the team lead, you are expected to mentor other engineers and lead them deliver high quality results that meet customer expectations.

israel.description:
About Flexport:

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.

Why Climate Matters More Than Ever

Supply chain leaders are being asked to cut costs and carbon at the same time. Yet logistics and sustainability teams often work with different data, tools, and priorities. Meanwhile, regulations and industry standards are raising expectations for how companies measure and manage their emissions.

Most climate tools stop at reporting: a dashboard or a year-end PDF, produced long after a shipment has moved. They rarely reach the people deciding how to route goods, when to ship, or how much inventory to hold.

The Climate team at Flexport is building emissions intelligence directly into the platform where supply chain decisions are made. We help customers weigh cost, speed, and emissions together—and turn that understanding into action.

The Opportunity

Flexport already runs the shipments, holds the data, and provides the platform where customers manage their supply chains. That puts us in a strong position to connect climate insights with the operational decisions that drive emissions.

You will be the primary engineer for Climate, working independently of our existing engineering teams and partnering closely with the Climate Manager, your main day-to-day business stakeholder.

Think of it as a small startup within Flexport: direct access to the business, a broad scope, and substantial ownership. Together with the Climate Manager, you will identify the most valuable problems to solve, shape the product direction, and turn ideas into reliable software. This role calls for someone who enjoys both deciding what to build and building it.

Things We ❤️

- Turning complex shipment and emissions data into clear, actionable choices.

- Working directly with stakeholders and users to understand what would make their lives better.

- Building simple, reliable products and learning from how people use them.

- Finding opportunities where lower costs and lower emissions go together.

- Taking an idea from an ambiguous problem to a useful product in production.

You Will

- Work closely with Climate Programs Manager to understand customer needs, challenge assumptions, and translate business goals into a practical product roadmap.

- Own delivery from problem discovery and technical design through implementation, launch, operation, and iteration.

- Build emissions intelligence into everyday supply chain decisions, including routing, transport mode, shipment timing, and inventory planning.

- Help customers identify opportunities to reduce emissions using Flexport’s shipment data.

- Make lower-emission choices easier to understand and act on within existing workflows.

- Develop products that help customers understand the wider environmental footprint of their supply chains, beyond freight.

- Deliver useful improvements incrementally, balancing speed, scope, maintainability, and data accuracy.

- Coordinate with other engineering teams when your work depends on shared systems, integrations, or expertise.

- Measure whether what you ship solves the underlying problem, and use that evidence to decide what comes next.

You Should Have

- 5+ years of software engineering experience, with a strong engineering foundation and experience delivering production software.

- A track record of working independently: you can bring structure to an unclear problem, set priorities, unblock yourself, and follow through without a detailed specification or constant direction.

- Strong product judgment: you understand user needs, identify what is worth building, and make thoughtful tradeoffs between impact and effort.

- Experience working closely with business stakeholders: you ask good questions, explain technical choices in plain language, and constructively challenge ideas when needed.

- The ability to own features across the stack, including user interfaces, backend services, and data integrations.

- A love of simple, well-tested code that is easy to extend and hard to break.

- Comfort taking responsibility for the reliability and maintenance of what you build.

- A bias for action, combined with the judgment to recognize when you need input or help.

- An aptitude for learning quickly, including unfamiliar business domains and technologies.

Nice to Have

- A personal motivation to work on climate and environmental challenges.

- Experience in climate technology, emissions accounting, logistics, or supply chain software.

- Experience building products in a startup or another small team with broad ownership.

- Experience turning complex data into customer-facing insights and decision tools.

Prior climate experience is a plus; curiosity and the ability to learn the domain matter more.

How We Work

- Your day-to-day work will center on a close partnership with the Climate Manager, with collaboration across engineering as needed.

- You will have substantial autonomy and will be expected to keep stakeholders aligned on priorities, progress, and tradeoffs.

- We build and launch incrementally, using feedback to guide the next step.

- In Amsterdam, we come to the office two to three times a week to collaborate, whiteboard, and spend time together.

- Flexport’s broader technology stack includes React, TypeScript, Ruby on Rails, Kotlin, Kubernetes, GraphQL, gRPC, Postgres, Kafka, and Snowflake. We welcome candidates from different technology backgrounds.

What’s in It for You?

- Direct ownership of products that help customers make better supply chain and environmental decisions.

- The opportunity to shape Climate technology with the autonomy of a small startup and the reach of Flexport.

- Equity participation and a defined pension contribution scheme.

- 25 vacation days based on full-time employment.

- Fully paid premiums for Flexport’s collective health insurance plan.

Senior Software Engineer: DevEx

Every engineer at Flexport ships code that moves real freight across 112 countries. The faster and safer they can do that, the faster the world's supply chains move. The PSI (Platform, Security & Infrastructure) team makes this possible: we build the paved path and tooling that hundreds of engineers around the world rely on every day to ship.

This is not a role where you wait for tickets. You'll talk to engineers, dogfood our platform, and find the friction that's slowing us down, and then design and ship the tools to remove that.

What You'll Do

You'll own and evolve the developer platform that powers Flexport engineering. That means:

- Making the best paved paths and self-serve tooling possible that make the right thing the easy thing.

- Creating and supporting developers with CI/CD pipelines (Buildkit, Github Actions), build tooling (Gradle, Bazel, npm/pnpm/bun, Go and Cargo) and artifact repositories (Artifactory, ECR, github).

- Owning and improving the backend and frontend developer experience.

- Acting as the steward of our GraphQL and gRPC ecosystem and make sure our middleware, federation and schema sharing, CLIs, codegen and servers and clients work smooth as butter.

- Evolving and integrating our IAM solutions and primitives so that everything is easy and secure by default.

- Making sure engineers can easily use and understand our container orchestration (Kubernetes, ECS) and observability stack (Openmetrics, Datadog) that engineers rely on to run, understand and debug their services.

You Should Have

- 5+ years of software engineering experience, with time spent building developer platforms, or internal tooling that other engineers depend on.

- Deep full-stack instincts: you're equally comfortable in a backend service, a frontend build pipeline, a Kubernetes manifest, and a CI configuration.

- Strong product instincts applied to internal users: you treat engineers as customers, identify what's actually worth building, and measure whether it worked.

- Expertise and hands on experience with several of: a CI/CD system (Github Actions preferred), a container orchestrator (Kubernetes preferred), build tooling preferably for more than one language, backend-for-frontend (Graphql preferred), service-to-service communication (gRPC preferred), Metrics and artifact storage.

- You take pride in solving tech debt and fixing what’s broken: you’ll either fix it, or if a migration is needed you either execute them yourself or make them feel effortless.

- An independent mindset: you thrive in ambiguity, find the highest-leverage problems yourself, and don't wait to be told what to do.

- Excellent communication: you can run a developer interview, write a clear design doc, and make sure everyone understands what’s going on.

- A generally helpful attitude. Everyone should know you within no-time as the person who gets stuff unblocked, points them in the right direction and makes their work easier.

- A drive for impact: you are not satisfying until every engineer is productive and confident thanks to your team.

Nice to Have

- Experience in data-driven DevX development using metrics such as DORA.

- Experience with AWS.

- Experience in Identity and Access Management (IAM) at scale such as JWTs, OIDC and fine-grained authorization.

- Experience with Terraform.

How We Work

- We come to the office 3 times a week to hang out, whiteboard, and ship together.

- We have the latest hardware and software, including frontier AI models on day one.

- We're agile, but not dogmatic. Teams decide how they work best.

Why This Role Is Special

- Massive leverage: every improvement you ship is multiplied across hundreds of engineers and thousands of deploys a day.

- Full ownership: from developer research to production rollout to measuring impact, it's yours.

- You shape the paved path: the conventions you set and decisions you make become how Flexport engineering builds for years to come.

What's in it for you:

- An opportunity to contribute to one of the fastest-growing companies, where you’ll have the chance to create a global impact while being a part of a  thriving multinational environment.

- Daily catered lunches incl. vegetarian options, breakfast, snacks and soft drinks available in our office on daily basis.

- Commute expenses: Flexport will cover  home-office commuting costs for employees living outside of Amsterdam.

- 25 working days as vacation days based on full time employment.

- Health insurance: Flexport offers a collective health insurance plan including a basic package and any available additional packages. Your monthly premium is fully paid by Flexport.

- A defined pension contribution scheme.

- Equity program: every team member becomes a shareholder, aligning our success with yours. As a private company in a multi-trillion dollar industry, you have a direct stake in our collective growth and success.

- Employee Assistance Program through Aetna Resources for Living: Flexport provides an employer-sponsored program at no cost to you and your household members.

- Parental leave benefit: Flexport is here to support you and your families in one of the most important times in life – the birth of a child! Our parental leave program allows both mothers and partners to take time off from work for pregnancy, childbirth, and to bond with your new child.

This role will require expertise in managing both direct-to-consumer (D2C) and business-to-business (B2B) fulfillment operations, with a hands-on approach to driving efficiency, cost reduction, and customer satisfaction. Leadership and Team Management:

- Provide strong leadership, guidance, and mentorship to the entire team, fostering a positive and productive work environment.

- Manage and develop a high-performing team of 300+ associates, including hiring, training, coaching, and performance management.

- Lead a team of 10 salaried employees, including department managers and supervisors, ensuring their success and alignment with organizational goals.

Operational Excellence:

- Oversee the day-to-day operations of the fulfillment center, ensuring efficient and accurate processing of orders, inventory management, and shipping for both D2C and B2B customers.

- Develop and implement operational strategies to optimize productivity, quality, and customer satisfaction.

- Establish operational distinctions for D2C vs. B2B fulfillment, ensuring proper flow paths, picking methodologies, and shipping requirements are met.

- Continuously monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) and operational metrics to drive continuous improvement and achieve operational targets.

- Foster a culture of safety, ensuring compliance with all applicable health and safety regulations and implementing measures to minimize workplace accidents and injuries.

- Develop and manage the fulfillment center's budget, ensuring financial objectives are met while maintaining operational excellence.

- Identify opportunities to optimize costs, reduce waste, and improve overall operational efficiency without compromising quality or service levels.

- Collaborate with other departments such as logistics, procurement, customer service, and quality control to ensure seamless coordination and integration of processes.

- Partner with the Regional General Manager to align fulfillment center strategies with overall company goals and objectives.

- Exceptional leadership and communication skills, with the ability to inspire and motivate teams to achieve goals.

- Proficiency in analyzing data, metrics, and KPIs to drive performance improvements.

- Solid financial acumen and experience in budgeting, cost management, and driving operational efficiency.

- Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment while maintaining attention to detail and ensuring accuracy.

- Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills, with a strategic mindset.

- Familiarity with warehouse management systems (WMS) and other relevant software applications.

- Knowledge of health and safety regulations and best practices in a warehousing environment.

The role

We're looking for a Social Media and Content Marketing Manager to own the channels where Flexport shows up every day. You'll run our social presence, keep the blog full of content people actually want to read, and produce a newsletter that logistics leaders look forward to opening. You'll write most of it yourself, polish the visuals in Canva, cut short videos for social, and build a network of voices, inside Flexport and out, who amplify our story.

This is a hands-on job for a strong writer who gets social, has an eye for design, and likes shipping work rather than just planning it.

You will

- Own Flexport's owned social channels day to day across LinkedIn, Twitter/X, YouTube, Facebook, and Instagram: plan the calendar, write the posts, publish, engage, and report on what's working.

- Write and edit blog content that turns complex supply chain topics into pieces people finish and share, from thought leadership to customer stories to product updates.

- Produce our newsletter end to end, from picking the stories to writing the copy to hitting send.

- Design social graphics and light marketing assets in Canva, staying true to Flexport's brand.

- Edit short-form video for social, including cutting clips, adding captions, and packaging them for each platform.

- Build our influencer network on both sides: coach internal experts and executives to post with confidence, and cultivate relationships with external creators and industry voices.

- Track performance across channels and use what you learn to make the next post, article, and newsletter better.

You should have

- 5+ years in social media, content marketing, or a closely related role.

- Genuinely strong writing. You can take a dense logistics topic and make it clear, sharp, and worth reading.

- Hands-on experience managing owned media channels, including LinkedIn, Twitter/X, YouTube, Facebook, and Instagram.

- A working command of social best practices across those platforms, from what to post to when and why, and how each channel differs.

- Basic design editing skills. You're comfortable building clean, on-brand graphics in Canva.

- Basic video editing skills. You can cut and caption short clips for social without needing a full production team.

- Comfort managing several channels and deadlines at once, with the ownership to keep them all moving.

- Bonus: experience building creator or influencer programs, or working in B2B, logistics, or tech.

israel.description:
About Flexport:

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.

The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.

The opportunity:

Flexport is a platform for global trade in an industry that comprises 12% of the global GDP.  We are the first licensed freight forwarder and customs brokerage built around a modern tech stack.  We help the world's fastest-growing brands manage their international supply chains, providing a fully-managed service for moving products between any two places on the planet.

Exceptional software development is integral in allowing us to fulfill our mission of fixing the user experience in global trade. At Flexport you’ll develop products that are at the forefront of reshaping the entire logistics & supply chain industries. You’ll work alongside self-starters interested in solving real-world problems and streamlining the inefficiencies in the complex global trade industry. You’ll have the opportunity to reshape an industry by creating the new operating system for global trade.

Our engineers are top-notch software developers who love listening to the users, working as a team, and proactively taking the lead whenever necessary. The role involves learning the business of freight forwarding, modeling the work that people do to move freight, designing solutions to make it more efficient, and thinking innovatively to automate much of it. In this role, you will have an opportunity to own the design and development of key parts of our forwarding systems. You will have influence on subsystem design and help contribute to a team culture around practices that are critical to a quality product.

About the team:

We have multiple teams in Shanghai and Shenzhen working on a suite of core products and services that enable Flexport operation to scale, including Forwarding Application, Client Application, Shipper Application, WMS, Consol Planning Tool, Document Platform (AI empowered), Email Platform, Compliance Platform, Work Assignment Engine, Exception Management, AI Copilot, Insight Builder (AI Data Analytics), Visibility & Schedules and so on.We are looking for engineers who love learning, are passionate about collaborating, and desire to build solutions with a global impact.

You will:

- Build highly available, secure, distributed systems in a microservice architecture.

- Design, develop, test and maintain systems that represent the real-world intricacies of logistics entities, such as shipper, client, cargo, document, carrier, container, email etc.

- Collaborate with some of the best engineers in the industry to work on complex business and technical problems.

- Build and launch products rapidly and incrementally. We ship to production dozens of times per day.

- Ensure our products maintain a high-quality bar. We believe in anticipating issues by obsessing over metrics and applying key learnings from post-mortems to all our services.

- Geek out about shipping and logistics. (We do this often.)

You should have:

Basic Qualifications

- 1+ years of experience writing software, and a strong engineering background.

- Knowledge of at least one programming language such as Ruby, C, C++, Java, or Kotlin

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or related technical field, or equivalent experience

Preferred Qualifications

- A love of simple, well-tested code that is easy to extend and hard to break.

- A bias for action. When you see a problem, you solve it.

- Knowledge of professional software engineering practices & best practices for full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, continuous deployments, testing, and operations

- Non-optional: an aptitude for learning quickly.

The Opportunity

Join our engineering team in Bellevue building and enhancing Flexport’s client-facing rates platform and self-serve freight booking experience. You will work alongside experienced engineers and have direct ownership of features that move the company from an assisted-sales model to a tech-run one for the long tail of our client base.

This team owns two of the highest-leverage surfaces in the Client App: how clients see pricing and how they book without manual intervention. Rates sit at the center of every freight decision, and you will build the systems that power rate visibility, quoting, and pricing intelligence across our ocean business. You will also help build the infrastructure that integrates AI-powered automation into the booking flow. This is a rare opportunity to build the "front door" of an $8.6 trillion industry, turning the complexity of global trade into a seamless digital experience for thousands of shippers.

You Will

- Design, develop, test, deploy, and maintain systems within a microservices architecture that power rate visibility and autonomous booking.

- Own the entire lifecycle of a feature: from database schema design and scalable backend APIs to building the React-based frontend applications our customers use.

- Support the integration of AI models and automated workflows to make the pricing and booking experience increasingly intelligent.

- Collaborate with engineering, product, and design to translate complex business problems into elegant, production-ready technical solutions.

- Contribute to code reviews to maintain high quality standards, share knowledge, and mentor peer engineers.

- Build highly available, secure, and distributed systems that can scale with Flexport’s global volume.

- Rapidly build and launch products incrementally, leveraging best practices around CI/CD and shipping to production dozens of times per day.

- Ensure high-quality standards by incorporating metrics, monitoring, and applying learnings from post-mortems to all services.

You Should Have

- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

- 3+ years of professional software engineering experience with a proven track record of shipping production-grade applications.

- Full-Stack Capability: You are comfortable owning a feature from end-to-end: working with databases, backend services (Java/Ruby), and frontend frameworks (React).

- Technical Rigor: A passion for simple, well-tested code that is easy to extend and hard to break.

- AI Familiarity: Experience or interest in working with AI APIs and building software that leverages machine learning models to automate user tasks.

- 2+ years of design and architecture knowledge as well as familiarity with object-oriented analysis and design patterns.

- Proficiency with modern programming languages: specifically Java, Ruby, or TypeScript.

- Proficiency with deploying, monitoring, and maintaining production services on cloud infrastructure (AWS).

It’s a Plus If You Have

- Experience with elements of our tech stack: Java, Spring Boot, Ruby on Rails, React, AWS.

- Experience in fintech, pricing engines, or booking systems.

- Experience in logistics, supply chain, or freight technology.

- A bias for action: When you see a problem, you fix it.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills: you can convey technical ideas in common terms to business stakeholders and product managers.

israel.title: Software Engineer II, DevEx
israel.description:
About Flexport:

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.

Software Engineer ll: DevEx

Every engineer at Flexport ships code that moves real freight across 112 countries. The faster and safer they can do that, the faster the world's supply chains move. The PSI (Platform, Security & Infrastructure) team makes this possible: we build the paved path and tooling that hundreds of engineers around the world rely on every day to ship.

As a Software Engineer II, you'll own well-scoped projects within our developer platform, typically working with a small group of teammates. You'll talk to the engineers who use our tools, dogfood the platform, and build a solid understanding of the problems and goals behind your work. Then you'll design and ship improvements that remove friction. You'll get support and guidance from senior engineers on the team while building real ownership of your projects from start to finish.

What You'll Do

You'll own projects within, and help evolve, the developer platform that powers Flexport engineering. That means:

- Building paved paths and self-serve tooling that make the right thing the easy thing.

- Building and supporting CI/CD pipelines (Buildkite, GitHub Actions), build tooling (Gradle, Bazel, npm/pnpm/bun, Go and Cargo) and artifact repositories (Artifactory, ECR, GitHub).

- Improving the backend and frontend developer experience through projects you scope and deliver.

- Contributing to our GraphQL and gRPC ecosystem: middleware, federation and schema sharing, CLIs, codegen, servers and clients.

- Contributing to our IAM solutions and primitives so that things are easy and secure by default.

- Helping engineers use and understand our container orchestration (Kubernetes, ECS) and observability stack (OpenMetrics, Datadog), so they can run, understand and debug their services.

- Gathering feedback from internal users, turning it into clear problem statements, and working with your team to prioritize what's worth building.

You Should Have

- 2-5 years of software engineering experience, ideally including time spent on developer platforms, internal tooling, or infrastructure that other engineers depend on.

- Full-stack curiosity: you're comfortable in a backend service and are building comfort across frontend build pipelines, Kubernetes manifests, and CI configuration.

- Hands-on experience with some of: a CI/CD system (GitHub Actions preferred), a container orchestrator (Kubernetes preferred), build tooling (more than one language is a plus), backend-for-frontend (GraphQL preferred), service-to-service communication (gRPC preferred), metrics, or artifact storage. You don't need all of them. You should be ready to learn the rest.

- A good grasp of problems and goals: you ask the right questions, understand who you're building for and why, and can explain how your work connects to broader team goals.

- Care for internal users: you treat engineers as customers, gather feedback, and check whether what you shipped actually helped.

- Ownership of your projects: you take a project from idea to production rollout, keep stakeholders informed, and raise risks early.

- Pride in fixing what's broken: you tackle tech debt in your area and help carry out migrations, with guidance on larger or cross-team efforts.

- Good communication: you can write a clear design doc for your project, take part in developer interviews, and keep your teammates up to date.

- A helpful attitude: you're the person who gets people unblocked and makes their work easier.

- Growth mindset: you seek out feedback, learn quickly, and are building toward broader scope and impact over time.

Nice to Have

- Exposure to data-driven DevX development using metrics such as DORA.

- Experience with AWS.

- Familiarity with Identity and Access Management (IAM) concepts such as JWTs, OIDC and fine-grained authorization.

- Experience with Terraform.

How We Work

- We come to the office 3 times a week to hang out, whiteboard, and ship together.

- We have the latest hardware and software, including frontier AI models on day one.

- We're agile, but not dogmatic. Teams decide how they work best.

Why This Role Is Special

- Real leverage: improvements you ship are used by hundreds of engineers and thousands of deploys a day.

- Meaningful ownership: you own your projects end to end, from developer research to production rollout to measuring impact.

- Room to grow: you'll work alongside senior engineers, get regular feedback, and build the skills to take on larger-scope work.

What's in it for you:

- An opportunity to contribute to one of the fastest-growing companies, where you’ll have the chance to create a global impact while being a part of a  thriving multinational environment.

- Daily catered lunches incl. vegetarian options, breakfast, snacks and soft drinks available in our office on daily basis.

- Commute expenses: Flexport will cover  home-office commuting costs for employees living outside of Amsterdam.

- 25 working days as vacation days based on full time employment.

- Health insurance: Flexport offers a collective health insurance plan including a basic package and any available additional packages. Your monthly premium is fully paid by Flexport.

- A defined pension contribution scheme.

- Equity program: every team member becomes a shareholder, aligning our success with yours. As a private company in a multi-trillion dollar industry, you have a direct stake in our collective growth and success.

- Employee Assistance Program through Aetna Resources for Living: Flexport provides an employer-sponsored program at no cost to you and your household members.

- Parental leave benefit: Flexport is here to support you and your families in one of the most important times in life – the birth of a child! Our parental leave program allows both mothers and partners to take time off from work for pregnancy, childbirth, and to bond with your new child.

israel.title: Staff Applied AI Engineer, Autonomous Supply Chains
israel.description:
About Flexport:

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.

The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.

Senior Applied AI Engineer, Autonomous Supply Chains

About Flexport

Look around you. Almost everything in the room crossed an ocean to get there. Moving one container from a factory to a warehouse takes 10 to 15 companies: truckers, customs brokers, port terminals, ocean carriers, insurers, lenders and warehouses, each with its own systems, paperwork and rules. A freight forwarder runs that whole journey, so the brand that makes the goods doesn't have to.

Most forwarders still run it on email, spreadsheets and phone calls. We call it email freight forwarding. Flexport runs it on one platform, where AI agents do the routine work and experts step in where judgment matters. We've moved $175B of goods for more than 13,000 brands across 135 countries. Our agents handle 21 million tasks a year, and up to 80% of customs work is automated.

Global logistics is a $13 trillion industry, and even the largest forwarder earns less than 3% of global logistics outsourcing revenue. People-powered operations don't scale: to grow, you hire. Software broke that ceiling for taxis with Uber, and for payments with Adyen and Stripe. Freight is next.

Amsterdam is one of Flexport's six engineering hubs, alongside San Francisco, Seattle, Chicago, Shanghai and Shenzhen. We own four domains end to end: Customs Technology, Autonomous Supply Chains (Applied AI), Platform and Security. See what we build at amsterdam-engineering.flexport.com.

The team: Autonomous Supply Chains

Logistics is famously hard to automate, because the happy path rarely happens. One customer won't take deliveries on a Tuesday. Another wants invoices only on Fridays, with some lines merged and others renamed. Until recently, people handled all of that by hand. Now operators use Forge, the agentic platform we build, to automate their own work: catching anomalies, routing exceptions, escalating stuck containers and adjusting invoices to each customer. Forge remembers every customer's rules and learns from every workflow run, so it gets smarter every day.

Autonomous Supply Chains is our Applied AI team: small, senior and reporting to the VP of Engineering. Self-driving cars are rated from level 0 to level 5. Most of the freight industry still runs at level 0: people emailing spreadsheets. Our goal is level 5 for freight, with Forge as the best agentic platform there is, handling every complexity, every calamity and every odd preference without skipping a beat.

Stack: TypeScript, Rust, Next.js, Temporal, Postgres and Snowflake, with models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Google.

The role

As a Staff Applied AI Engineer on Autonomous Supply Chains, you'll set the direction for the agents that run real logistics work. You'll find the highest-leverage problems in our operations, decide what's worth building, design the solution and ship it to operators moving freight across 135 countries. Nobody hands you a spec, and nobody needs to.

What you'll do

- Set the technical direction for Forge: how its agents plan, remember, use tools and hand off to people.

- Design and ship end-to-end AI agents that handle real logistics work, such as customs compliance, document processing, invoice validation and exception management.

- Build the evaluation, guardrails and human-in-the-loop flows that make an agent trustworthy enough to run 24/7.

- Stay on top of what's happening in the world of AI, and channel those innovations straight into the product. When Jev came out this fall, we had three use cases live within two weeks.

- Work directly with operators, domain experts and leadership to turn ambiguous problems into shipped products, and measure whether they worked.

- Cross organizational boundaries to understand problems deeply, align stakeholders and get things done without waiting for permission.

- Raise the bar for the team through design reviews, mentoring and the patterns other engineers build on.

You should have

- 10+ years of software engineering experience, and you've built seriously with LLMs, whether in production, in side projects or just because you couldn't stop yourself.

- LLM fluency: agent patterns, tool use, RAG, prompt design and evaluation. You know the difference between what works in production and what looks good in a demo.

- Full-stack capability in TypeScript and Next.js. You can own a feature end to end.

- Product instinct: you can tell what's worth building, not just how to build it.

- A track record of leading ambiguous, cross-team technical work from idea to production.

- Clear written and spoken communication in English, including design docs that people actually read.

Nice to have

- Experience with workflow orchestration, such as Temporal.

- Experience building internal tools or operator-facing applications.

How we work

- We value builders. People who think end to end, do their own discovery and ship independently. Nobody hands you a spec.

- Your users sit next to you. Operators, customs experts and account teams work in the same office. Watch them use your tool, and fix it before dessert.

- Any model, any harness. Use any frontier model from Anthropic, OpenAI or Google, in all the popular coding harnesses. Our engineers manage swarms of coding agents from their first week.

- We ship dozens of times a day, with continuous deployment and a platform team obsessed with making it safe and fast.

- Hybrid, in English. We're together in our office on Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal, a few minutes from Dam Square, three days a week*. The other days are flexible. English is our working language, and we work daily with colleagues in the US and China.

- No logistics background needed. Almost nobody joins knowing what an HTS code or a bill of lading is. The experts sit a few desks away.

- Agile, but not dogmatic. Teams decide how they work best.

Why this role is special

- Your work is visible: a small, senior team that reports to the VP of Engineering. What you build gets noticed, and your ideas set the direction.

- Real stakes: your agents act on real shipments for 13,000+ brands in 135 countries, so the impact is immediate and measurable.

- You're early: the playbook for applied AI in logistics hasn't been written yet. You'll help write it.

What's in it for you

- Equity for everyone: every team member becomes a shareholder in a pre-IPO company in a multi-trillion dollar industry.

- 25 vacation days, based on full-time employment, plus Dutch public holidays.

- Health insurance, fully paid: a collective plan with basic and additional packages. Flexport pays the monthly premium.

- Pension: a defined contribution scheme.

- Breakfast and lunch: daily catered lunch with vegetarian options, breakfast, snacks and drinks in the office.

- Commute covered: Flexport covers home-to-office commuting costs if you live outside Amsterdam.

- Parental leave: time off for both parents to bond with a new child.

- Wellbeing support: an Employee Assistance Program through Aetna for you and your household, at no cost.

- Visa sponsorship: we sponsor visas for the right candidates and help you move to Amsterdam. Eligible international hires may also benefit from the Dutch expat tax ruling.

Our hiring process

- Application review: our team reviews your application.

- Recruiter screen: talk about your experience, the role and your questions about Flexport.

- Hiring manager screen: an initial conversation with the hiring manager.

- Remote live coding: a live coding interview over video.

- Onsite coding and system design: coding and system design interviews in our office.

- Project deep dive: discuss a project from your experience with the hiring manager.

- Team debrief: the interview team reviews feedback together. You don't attend this step.

- Offer: if there's a match, your recruiter walks you through the offer.



Your recruiter will confirm the plan before interviews begin. We only contact candidates from @flexport.com addresses, and we will never ask you for money or banking details.
