remote.title: VP Technology Pre Sales & Client Solutioning Lead
remote.description:
Job Summary
The Technology Pre-Sales & Client Solutioning Leader is responsible for championing the Technology Pre-Sales practice, supporting Sales and Front-End teams in identifying and securing new business opportunities across multiple industries and international geographies. This role focuses on designing innovative, data and AI-powered solutions, developing competitive pricing models, and ensuring seamless client onboarding and technology transitions. The position is pivotal in driving our client's growth through strategic solutioning, stakeholder management, and cross-functional leadership.
Key Responsibilities

- Drive the maturity and effectiveness of Technology Pre-Sales practice by identifying and implementing domain-specific, data & AI-powered solutions through market research and innovation.

- Serve as the lead Technology SPOC, collaborating closely with Sales, Business Growth, and Front-End teams throughout the sales lifecycle (RFI, RFP, due diligence, client presentations).

- Develop and deliver compelling technical presentations, solution descriptions, and graphical diagrams for prospective clients as part of client due diligence.

- Lead and engage in client presentations, due diligence sessions, customer checkpoints, and management/legal reviews.

- Manage end-to-end RFI/RFP processes, providing high-level, client-specific technology solution designs, cost estimates, implementation timelines, and responses to due diligence and security questionnaires.

- Mentor and provide on-the-job training to colleagues and team members, fostering a culture of continuous learning and excellence.

- Lead the gathering of business requirements and collaborate with Technology Subject Matter Experts, partners, and OEMs to design complex, client-specific technology solutions.

- Travel as required with migration and sales teams to meet clients, understand their environments, assess their needs, and present tailored solutions.

- Independently manage RFI/RFP responses, ensuring solutions are aligned with client requirements and business objectives.

- Prepare and submit comprehensive costing and pricing inputs in line with proposed solutions.

- Oversee technology project management, enablement, and integration, ensuring projects follow a structured process from initiation to closure.

- Collaborate with commercial and legal teams to ensure all technology elements are accurately captured in MSAs and SoWs.

- Ensure cost management for new client onboarding, including identification, approval, tracking, and reporting of technology enablement costs.

- Lead technology onboarding and transitions for new client engagements, managing cross-functional technology teams in complex, project-based environments.

- Effectively manage internal and external stakeholders, ensuring delivery of all project milestones and final deliverables within budget and timelines.

- Serve as the primary liaison to project management team, proactively communicating project status, risks, and issues.

- Conduct solution reviews and oversee all project-related quality initiatives to ensure the timeliness and quality of deliverables.

- Ensure complete documentation of client-specific technology policies and procedures, aligned with our client's business interests, and oversee their implementation.

- Manage key internal and external interactions.

Qualifications

- Bachelors or masters degree in computer science, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field.

- 10 years of experience in technology pre-sales, solution architecture, or a related field, preferably in a global or multi-industry environment.

- Proven expertise in designing and delivering data & AI-powered solutions; strong understanding of technology pricing, costing, and commercial models.

- Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams and manage complex projects from initiation to closure.

- Experience managing senior internal and external stakeholders, including clients, partners, and vendors.

- Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to present complex technical solutions to both technical and non-technical audiences.

- Familiarity with legal and commercial aspects of technology engagements, including MSAs, SoWs, and compliance requirements.

- Strong mentoring and team development skills, with a track record of providing on-the-job training and fostering a collaborative culture.

- Willingness and ability to travel internationally as required.

remote.title: Technical Product Manager - AI Neobank
remote.description:
About BJAK
The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.
The Role
BJAK is building a AI Neobank Superapp for Southeast Asia across payments, remittance, insurance, wealth, and trading.
These products move real money. Reliability, regulatory requirements, and third-party financial rails are fundamental to the product - not considerations around the edges.
The Technical Product Manager owns a product vertical end-to-end, from strategy and outcomes through technical design, delivery, and launch.
We are AI-native by default, but AI is a means, not the goal. The bar is knowing where AI genuinely improves an outcome, where deterministic systems must remain in control, and how to build products that are reliable, auditable, and trusted.
What You'll Own

- Owning a product vertical end-to-end, including strategy, metrics, roadmap, priorities and delivery.

- Shaping technical design with engineering across APIs, data flows, ledgering, reconciliation, failure handling, security and scalability.

- Driving trade-offs across correctness, speed, cost, reliability, regulatory requirements and user experience.

- Building regulatory requirements into the product across KYC, transaction monitoring, limits, privacy and licensing.

- Applying AI where it improves outcomes, with clear evaluation, safeguards, human oversight and failure handling.

- Shipping products around external dependencies, including regulatory approvals, financial rails and third-party partners.

- Aligning Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance around clear product decisions and launch requirements.

What We're Looking For

- 5+ years of product management experience, including ownership of complex technical products from strategy through production.

- Strong technical foundation across system architecture, APIs, databases, workflows, failure modes and distributed systems.

- Experience working closely with engineers and ability to review, challenge and contribute to technical designs.

- Experience in payments, banking, remittance, insurance, trading or another regulated, high-consequence product domain.

- Strong product judgment and ability to make difficult trade-offs under technical, regulatory and operational constraints.

- Experience building with LLMs or AI products, including evaluation, reliability and understanding when AI should not be used.

Nice to have

- Engineering or highly technical product background.

- Experience building zero-to-one fintech or consumer products.

- Experience defining evaluation frameworks for ML or LLM-powered products.

Outcome

- Clear vertical strategy and legible roadmap

- Ships fast and clears the gates that actually block launch

- Money is correct and users are never misled about the state of their funds

- AI features are valuable, predictable and trusted

- Trade-offs made deliberately under uncertainty and hold up when challenged

- Engineering, design, compliance, and operations are aligned with minimal friction

Location
This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our local office at least 3 days per week, with the remaining days offering flexibility to work remotely.
Candidates should be based in, or able to work from, the location where the role is advertised.
Language
English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.
Interview Process
Our process is designed to move fast:

- Online assessment or practical task

- Technical interview

- CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

remote.company: Americans United for Separation of Church and State
remote.description:
Americans United for Separation of Church and State is seeking full-time summer legal interns who are committed to civil rights, impact litigation, and upholding core First Amendment protections.
About Americans United. Americans United is a nonpartisan educational and advocacy organization dedicated to advancing the constitutional principle of church-state separation as the only way to ensure freedom of religion, including the right to believe or not believe, for all of us. Founded in 1947, Americans United is a diverse and dynamic organization composed of people from all walks of life: lawyers and lobbyists, students and activists, religious leaders and impassioned Americans. Americans United includes people of faith and people who don’t profess any particular faith.
For nearly 80 years, we have litigated church-state issues in federal and state courts across the country, with a substantial practice before the federal courts of appeals and the U.S. Supreme Court. Most of our cases involve novel, cutting-edge First Amendment and other constitutional issues. In recent years, for example, we have litigated lawsuits and submitted amicus briefs challenging or opposing:

- Coercive religious practices in the public schools.

- Proselytizing by Trump-Vance Administration officials.

- Public funding of religious education.

- Religion-based refusals by businesses, foster-care agencies, and government officials to provide services to LGBTQ+ people and religious minorities.

- Religion-based efforts to deprive people of access to abortion and contraceptives.

- Race-based and sex-based employment discrimination by religious employers.

For more information about Americans United’s legal program, please visit our website at .
Duties and responsibilities. Legal interns receive substantive legal experience with in-depth exposure to some of the most important issues facing the nation. Interns assist with ongoing litigation by conducting legal and factual research and writing, analyze potential new litigation, and draft demand letters to resolve constitutional violations without filing suit. Interns may also draft pleadings, briefs, or discovery.
Our attorneys endeavor to prepare interns for public-interest legal practice, including by providing training and practical experience, in house and in conjunction with partner organizations. Interns are encouraged to take full advantage of the many events that take place in Washington, D.C., or are available virtually.
Eligibility and requirements. Law students (any year) who are committed to advancing the public interest and the separation of religion and government are encouraged to apply. Americans United includes and welcomes people of all genders, races, ethnicities, religions and beliefs, sexual orientations, gender identities, ages, socioeconomic backgrounds, and abilities. Because we work on a wide variety of issues and with many different communities, we value what diversity and diverse perspectives bring to our work.
Research shows candidates from marginalized groups are less likely to apply for positions when they don’t meet 100% of the listed requirements; please consider applying even if you don’t match 100% of these criteria.
Equal opportunity employer. Americans United is an equal opportunity employer. We consider applicants without regard to race, color, religion, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, marital or veteran status, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected status. If you need an accommodation for a disability to apply to this position, please let us know by emailing .
Compensation: A stipend of $7,360 for a ten-week term.
Work Location: Interns can work remotely from anywhere in the United States. There may also be opportunities to work in person in our Washington, D.C. office.
Working conditions and physical requirements. This position primarily involves working from a home office and/or professional office environment. The position requires routinely using standard office equipment such as computers, phones, and video-conferencing tools. It also requires the ability to remain in a stationary position for extended periods, communicate effectively, and occasionally move about within the workspace.
How to apply.Please submit a cover letter, resume, law-school transcript, writing sample, and a list of three references through our web-based application portal at . The cover letter should highlight why you want to work with us and what perspectives you would bring to strengthen our practice. The writing sample may be of any length; it should be your best example of comprehensive and detailed legal argument or analysis, should be your own work, and should not be substantially edited by anyone else. First-year law students who apply before receipt of their initial grades may submit a law-school transcript that shows their initial courses and an undergraduate transcript. If you have any questions about an internship position, please do not hesitate to contact us at .
Deadline: Positions will remain open until filled. Applicants are encouraged to apply by October 15, 2026.

ABOUT THE JOB
Build a new market in the industry you already know.
Our client is a fast-growing outsourcing company that builds dedicated remote teams for US businesses. Their people handle customer support, sales support, scheduling, admin, and back-office work inside the client’s own systems, as part of the client’s team. They became a known name in two niche industries by learning those businesses deeply, and the model worked well enough that they’re now taking it into new markets, starting with an acquisition that opens the door to real estate.
They’re hiring one or two Vice Presidents of Business Development to lead that expansion. Each VP owns a vertical: Real Estate, Home Services and Construction, Waste Management and Environmental Services, or Hospitality. You’ll build the go-to-market from the ground up: who to call, what to offer them, how to price and package it, and how to turn the first few clients into a reputation. You’ll report to the Senior Vice President of Sales and work alongside Marketing and Customer Experience. Our client is clear about who will thrive in this role, and who won’t.
They’re not looking for someone who has spent their career selling staffing, outsourcing, or BPO services. They’re not looking for a strategist who needs a team to execute, or an account manager who’s most comfortable growing relationships someone else opened.
They’re seeking an industry insider: someone who has spent years in real estate, home services or construction, waste and environmental services, or hospitality, running part of the business or selling into it, who knows the owners and operators by name and understands where the work piles up: the phones, the scheduling, the paperwork, the follow-up that never gets done. You can sit across from a CEO and talk about their business, not about outsourcing. You don’t need to have sold a service like this before. They’ll teach you the offering. You bring the industry.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

- Own new business for your vertical, from first conversation to signed agreement, with a pipeline you build yourself

- Design the go-to-market for a new industry: the ideal client profile, the offer, the pricing conversation, and the partnerships that open doors

- Land strategic partnerships and national accounts, then deepen them

- Be the face of the company in your industry: conferences, trade associations, client visits, and the dinners where deals get started

- Work with Marketing and Customer Experience so what you sell is what gets delivered, and what you hear in the market shapes the offer

- Help set the strategic direction of the division as the new verticals take hold

IDEAL PROFILE

- 5+ years in B2B business development with deep relationships in one of the target industries: real estate, home services and construction, waste management and environmental services, or hospitality

- 5+ years in senior sales leadership with a track record of winning in that industry, or selling into it

- Comfortable building and managing relationships with owners and the C-suite

- Experience in high-growth environments, using data and technology to drive results

- An entrepreneur’s mindset: strategic enough to design the plan, hands-on enough to run it

- Collaborative, efficient, and motivated by results; you want to win the day

- Energized by networking and industry events

- Bachelor’s degree in business, management, communication, or a related field

- Strong written and spoken communication; tech-savvy and quick to adopt new tools

- Not required: any background in outsourcing, staffing, or BPO

LOCATION & WORK MODEL

- Remote, anywhere in the US

- Core hours Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM Central

- Travel for industry events, conferences, and client meetings

COMPENSATION
Base salary: $135,000 to $150,000, plus commission

remote.title: Product Manager On-Ramp & Swap (100% remote)
remote.description:
Join Tether and Shape the Future of Digital Finance
At Tether, we’re not just building products, we’re pioneering a global financial revolution. Our cutting-edge solutions empower businesses—from exchanges and wallets to payment processors and ATMs—to seamlessly integrate reserve-backed tokens across blockchains. By harnessing the power of blockchain technology, Tether enables you to store, send, and receive digital tokens instantly, securely, and globally, all at a fraction of the cost. Transparency is the bedrock of everything we do, ensuring trust in every transaction.
Innovate with Tether
Tether Finance: Our innovative product suite features the world’s most trusted stablecoin, USDT, relied upon by hundreds of millions worldwide, alongside pioneering digital asset tokenization services.
But that’s just the beginning:
Tether Power: Driving sustainable growth, our energy solutions optimize excess power for Bitcoin mining using eco-friendly practices in state-of-the-art, geo-diverse facilities.
Tether Data: Fueling breakthroughs in AI and peer-to-peer technology, we reduce infrastructure costs and enhance global communications with cutting-edge solutions like KEET, our flagship app that redefines secure and private data sharing.
Tether Education: Democratizing access to top-tier digital learning, we empower individuals to thrive in the digital and gig economies, driving global growth and opportunity.
Tether Evolution: At the intersection of technology and human potential, we are pushing the boundaries of what is possible, crafting a future where innovation and human capabilities merge in powerful, unprecedented ways.
Why Join Us?
Our team is a global talent powerhouse, working remotely from every corner of the world. If you’re passionate about making a mark in the fintech space, this is your opportunity to collaborate with some of the brightest minds, pushing boundaries and setting new standards. We’ve grown fast, stayed lean, and secured our place as a leader in the industry.
If you have excellent English communication skills and are ready to contribute to the most innovative platform on the planet, Tether is the place for you.
Are you ready to be part of the future?
About the job
Tether Wallet is our self-custodial wallet, built to bring USDT and XAUT directly to the people who rely on Tether every day, especially in markets where access to stable money and savings is hardest. For that to work, getting into these assets has to be simple, fast and affordable. Our goal is to give every Tether Wallet user the best option to exchange any local currency or token into USDT and XAUT, wherever they are.
In this role, you will define and own the strategy for buying and swapping into USDT and XAUT across our target markets. You will work hand in hand with our expansion teams to map the payment landscape in each market: which payment methods people actually use, which card schemes and bank rails dominate, and which on-ramp and swap providers can serve them. Based on that, you will identify the best partner for each market and bring them on board as a service partner of Tether Wallet.
This role sits at the intersection of product, payments and partnerships. You will own the outcome end to end, from the first partner evaluation through integration and the in-app experience to the conversion numbers after launch. If you enjoy turning a fragmented global payments landscape into a buy button that just works, we want to hear from you.
Key responsibilities:

- Buy & Swap Strategy: Define and own the strategy and roadmap for buying and swapping into USDT and XAUT in Tether Wallet, covering fiat on-ramps, card payments, local payment methods and token-to-token swaps.

- Market & Payment Landscape: Work with our expansion teams to build a deep understanding of each target market, including dominant payment methods, card schemes, bank transfer and instant payment rails, mobile money, local regulation, and the on-ramp and swap providers active there.

- Partner Evaluation & Selection: Define clear evaluation criteria such as market and payment method coverage, fees and FX spreads, approval and conversion rates, KYC experience, settlement speed, reliability and compliance standing, and use them to select the best on-ramp or swap partner for each market.

- Partner Onboarding: Lead selected partners from evaluation to go-live as service partners of Tether Wallet, coordinating with Legal, Compliance and Business Development on due diligence, commercial terms and contracts.

- Integration & Delivery: Translate partner capabilities and APIs into clear product requirements, user stories and acceptance criteria, and work with engineering and design to deliver a seamless in-app buy and swap experience.

- Routing & Optimization: Define the logic that decides which partner and payment method a user is offered based on country, currency, amount, price and availability, so every user gets the best available option.

- Performance & Partner Management: Define and track KPIs across the buy and swap funnel, such as conversion, payment approval rates, KYC drop-off, total cost to the user and volume by market and partner. Use the data to improve the experience, manage partner performance and incidents, and regularly review whether each market still has the right partner.

Requirements
Mandatory:

- 5+ years of product management experience in the financial industry (banking, payment service provider, FinTech)

- 3+ years of product management experience in DeFi or crypto industry

- Good understanding of crypto wallets and DeFi features, including token swaps, DEX aggregators and on-chain transaction flows.

- Good understanding of global payment systems and credit card schemes (e.g. Visa, Mastercard), including authorization, 3-D Secure and chargebacks, as well as local payment methods such as bank transfers, instant payment rails and mobile money.

- Hands-on experience with fiat on-ramp, off-ramp or swap providers, or with integrating third-party payment providers and gateways into a consumer product.

- Proven experience evaluating, selecting and onboarding external partners, and managing their performance after launch.

- Working knowledge of KYC/AML requirements and how they affect user onboarding and conversion.

- Technical enough to read partner API documentation, assess integration options and work closely with engineering teams.

- Data-driven: experience defining funnel KPIs and using data to improve conversion and make partner decisions.

- Excellent communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with partners, expansion teams and engineers across time zones in a remote environment.

Important information for candidates
Recruitment scams have become increasingly common. To protect yourself, please keep the following in mind when applying for roles:

- Apply only through our official channels. We do not use third-party platforms or agencies for recruitment unless clearly stated. All open roles are listed on our official careers page:

- Own a vertical end-to-end - outcomes and metrics, a backlog prioritised by value / risk / dependency / strategic priority, acceptance criteria crisp enough to build and test against.

- Shape the technical design with engineering - system boundaries, money-movement correctness (idempotency, ledgering, reconciliation), third-party-rail reliance and rail-down behaviour, failure/retry/refund paths, security, latency, scalability, recovery.

- Make hard trade-offs across correctness, speed, cost, reliability and UX - and defend them to an engineering, compliance or ops lead who pushes back.

- Treat regulated constraints as first-class product inputs - licensing scope, CDD/KYC and limits, sanctions/PEP screening, transaction monitoring, data residency and privacy. Know which are hard launch gates and which are forward-readiness.

- Apply AI where it earns its place - define what it's allowed to decide, where a human stays in the loop, how it's evaluated, and what it does when unsure. Every AI-surfaced number traces back to a real record.

- Ship against external gates - build feature-complete behind flags; go live per rail as each partner and regulatory gate clears.

- Work across Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance/Reconciliation

What We're Looking For

- Product leadership - significant experience owning a complex technical product end-to-end; strong judgement and decisiveness under ambiguity; ability to balance ambition against technical, regulatory and operational reality; can hold their own with senior engineers.

- Technical foundation - solid system design (boundaries, datastores, queues/workflows, APIs, failure modes, consistency under concurrency); comfort reading, reviewing and challenging design docs; can sketch an architecture and a sequence. No production code, but technical enough that engineers don't have to simplify.

- Domain - experience in a regulated / high-consequence domain (payments, banking, remittance, insurance, …) or demonstrable fast-ramp ability; understands why money movement is different (correctness over convenience, irreversible states, partners you don't control).

- AI judgement - hands-on with LLM-based products; can frame a feature as eval-able (offline, online, human feedback); realistic on hallucination/drift/data gaps, including data-blocked vs model-blocked and when a model must not be in the loop at all.

- Nice to have - engineer or highly-technical-PM background · zero-to-one · shipped AI-heavy consumer products · defined eval metrics for ML/LLM systems · AI UX + failure-handling intuition · SEA market experience.

Outcome

- Clear vertical strategy and legible roadmap

- Ships fast and clears the gates that actually block launch

- Money is correct and users are never misled about the state of their funds

- AI features are valuable, predictable and trusted

- Trade-offs made deliberately under uncertainty and hold up when challenged

- Engineering, design, compliance, and operations are aligned with minimal friction

This is a remote role. We hire globally and work across multiple countries and time zones.
Candidates should be comfortable working effectively in a distributed, fast-moving international team and collaborating with colleagues across different locations.
Language
English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.
Interview Process
Our process is designed to move fast:

- Online assessment or practical task

- Technical interview

- CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

About the job
is a general purpose AI assistant that runs locally on your devices. It gives people real control over their data and how they use AI. No cloud dependency, no data harvesting, and no one else's servers between you and your assistant. Our focus is local, on-device, privacy-preserving AI, connected across Tether's peer-to-peer ecosystem. We're building the AI assistant people actually own. Product sets the direction.
We're looking for a Product Engineering Lead to turn that direction into features people love, built to a standard that holds up on real devices with real constraints. You lead the teams that build QV.AC's features and app experience on top of our local AI stack, each with its own lead. You report directly to the CTO and take direction from product. Product owns the what and the why. You own the how and the engineering bar.
The split is roughly 70% engineering leadership and 30% product. You're a combination of three things. You're an engineering leader who has helped teams ship consumer products at speed. You have real product sense and can partner with PMs as an equal, shaping what gets built, not just executing it. And you have an intuition for AI systems and their limits, so you can turn emerging capabilities into features that work reliably on-device, without needing to build the models yourself.
Responsibilities

- Engineering - Run the app and feature teams day to day: unblocking, reviewing, and keeping them shipping.- Set and hold a high engineering bar for performance, reliability, and clean APIs.- Own the technical design of features and the API surface between our AI core and the app.- Make sure your teams work closely with our AI research and deep tech teams on code reviews, design, and anything that touches models or inference.

- Product Partnership - Work alongside QV.AC's product managers to turn vision and roadmap into scoped, buildable work.- Push back when scope and reality don't match, and propose better paths when they exist.- Bring an engineering perspective to product decisions, especially on what local models can do well today and what they can't yet.- Help the team move fast, using AI tools and quick prototypes to validate ideas before committing to them.

- Leadership - Create clarity around team goals and make sure everyone knows what success looks like.- Mentor team leads to build strong team operating systems, improve how their teams work with others, and grow as leaders.- Lead by example: roll up your sleeves when the team needs it, and step back when they're ready to own it.

Requirements
Mandatory:

- Experience managing engineers or engineering leads who ship consumer product, ideally AI-powered apps.

- Strong product sense: you can tell a good feature from a busy one.

- Intuition for applied AI and on-device constraints: model size, latency, memory, battery, and the gap between a good demo and a reliable feature. You don't need ML research expertise, because our core abstracts it away.

- You use AI tools heavily in your own work and enjoy experimenting with new models and capabilities.

- Deep JavaScript and React.

- Initiative, curiosity, resilience, and the ability to give and receive direct critique.

Preferred:

- Bonus: Experience with local or on-device inference, LLM evals, cross-platform mobile and desktop apps, or open source.

There are over 5 billion users using basic applications today such email, notes, tasks, calendar and they're not AI-native. Our mission is to build proactive applications for anyone in the world, who are not used to complex prompting. We aim to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal to no prompting.
Our first application is an agent-first mobile communication app. We believe building applications that users use daily for communication, coordination and collaboration needs will help integrate AI into their lives. The net effect is to eliminate misinformation, achieve low coordination costs, enable high quality tasks and collaboration at scale with minimal or little prompting.
As Engineering Lead, AI Email App, you own the engineering layer that turns AI capability into a reliable product. You will shape the architecture across backend services, APIs, and client applications, while leading a small team of senior engineers.
This is a hands-on leadership role. You stay close to the code, make critical architectural decisions, and ensure the system remains fast, reliable, and coherent as it scales.
What You'll Own

- Own the application engineering strategy and execution across backend, mobile, and desktop.

- Design reliable systems for AI-powered workflows, including state, orchestration, tool use, retries, fallbacks, and failure handling.

- Build the APIs and abstractions that connect AI systems to real-world product experiences.

- Lead a small, senior engineering team and raise the technical bar through design reviews, code reviews, and hands-on mentorship.

- Make high-impact trade-offs across latency, reliability, cost, security, and user experience.

- Establish strong production foundations: observability, monitoring, testing, and operational excellence.

- Partner closely with ML leadership to turn model capabilities into robust, shippable product experiences.

- Move quickly while keeping the architecture simple, maintainable, and ready to scale.

What We're Looking For

- Significant experience leading application or product engineering for complex systems.

- Strong hands-on background building and shipping backend systems used in production.

- Experience building AI-powered products or systems that integrate with modern ML/LLM capabilities.

- Strong technical judgment and the ability to make decisions with incomplete information.

- Comfortable working across backend and client platforms, with deep expertise in at least one.

- A strong bias toward ownership, shipping, and learning from real-world usage.

- High standards for code quality, reliability, and engineering fundamentals.

Outcomes

- Production systems are observable, monitored, and stable under real-world load.

- Decisions consistently balance speed, cost, reliability, and user experience.

- Features across backend, mobile, and desktop work smoothly and reliably.

- Latency and reliability improve measurably over time.

How We Work
We are a small, high-talent-density, hands-on team. Engineers have broad ownership and are expected to exercise strong judgment and execute independently.

remote.title: Performance Creative Strategist, Contract
remote.description:
About Mass Culture

Mass Culture is a growth media agency. We help mission-driven scale-ups connect brand and performance so they grow faster, more profitably, and with purpose.

About the Role

Mass Culture helps brands grow with intention and integrity by closing the gap between brand and performance. Our sister agency, Brains, makes brands people choose, not just consider. This role stands right between the two, which is a great place to stand if you like knowing why things work.

You read the account, with data and intuition. You find what's working, what's tired, and what nobody has tried yet. You get to know the human needs behind the numbers, map the gaps, and decide what we test next. Then you write the brief, and Brains takes it through a full creative process and makes it real. You don't design or edit the ads. You decide what they need to do, and how we'll know if they did it.

This job done well is a flywheel: performance signal in, sharper (and more importantly bolder) creative out, and better signal back. Done badly, it's a deck about a deck that produces boring creative that’s been done before. We’re hiring you for the first one.

What You'll Own

-
Creative diagnosis: read creative performance across Meta, TikTok, YouTube, and the rest, and say plainly what's working, what's fatiguing, and why. Hook rate, hold rate, CTR, CPA, ROAS, and MER are working tools here, not a vocabulary test.

-
The people behind the numbers: build the persona and angle work for each account. Who we're talking to, what they believe, what stops the scroll, and which angles we haven't tried yet. Nobody owes a brand their attention, so we go earn it.

-
The testing roadmap: every concept carries a hypothesis, every launch gets a readout, and every readout changes what we brief next. Test it, learn it, write it down.

-
Briefs: write briefs the creative team can run with, no decoder ring required. The problem, the audience, the angle, the hook, the proof, the formats, and the platform specs.

-
The bridge: be the person media and creative both trust, and both actually call. You give media a clear read on the creative, and give creative the context to make its best work.

-
Learning that travels: what we learn on one account should make the next one smarter. Keep the angle library, and bring it to every brief.

-
Client conversations: present creative findings in QBRs and working sessions alongside account and media leads. Explain the why. Skip the abracadabra.

How We Work Together

-
Mass owns the why, Brains owns the how. You set direction and define success. The creative team runs concepting and production. Push the work, and respect the craft.

-
Growth is the only proof. Beautiful ads that don't move the business are a magic show. We're not great at magic shows.

-
Platform first, then pretty. If a format has constraints, the brief says so up front, so the work gets built right the first time.

-
Bring the numbers. You'll have our client portal and the analysis tools behind it. Opinions are welcome. Opinions with data get built.

-
Say when something is wrong, including when it's a brief you wrote. Safe is expensive. So is staying quiet when a good bet just doesn’t pay off.

What We're Looking For

Required

- 3 to 6 years in performance creative strategy, agency-side or at a high-growth DTC brand.

- Real fluency with Meta creative and Ads Manager, and working knowledge of TikTok and YouTube. You can open an account and tell the story of what the creative is doing.

- Briefs that turned into ads that scaled, and the ability to explain exactly why. Luck happens. We'll want to know what wasn't luck.

- Direct-response instincts: hooks, angles, awareness levels, offers, and proof.

- Experience running structured creative testing, not just launching variations and hoping.

- Clear writing. Most of this job is a brief, a readout, or a recommendation.

- An ad you were sure about that lost, and what you changed because of it. We will ask. We'll tell you one of ours, too.

Nice to Have

- Experience in supplements, wellness, CPG, or other subscription and continuity categories.

- Creative analytics tools like Motion, Triple Whale, or whatever you swear by.

- Briefing UGC creators and influencer content.

- Amazon creative: A+ content, Brand Store, and Sponsored Brands video.

- Experience partnering with a brand-led creative agency.

- A non-traditional path. Ex-founders, recovering copywriters, and media buyers who got curious about the creative are all welcome here.

Engagement

Contract, remote, and ongoing, starting at 20 to 30 hours a week across a focused set of accounts. Rate is agreed up front. If it's working for both sides, there's room to grow into a full-time role.

To apply, send a note and two or three briefs or creative readouts you're proud of, with the results. Real numbers, please.

Why Mass Culture

We are not a traditional agency. We work inside our clients' businesses, connect media to margins, and measure ourselves on their growth, not our output. Our sister company, Brains, is a world-class branding agency, and that relationship is real. We love brand as much as we love performance.

Senior people do actual work here. We spend a client's money like we made it. And we still see our families and have book clubs and such.

No hacking. No smoke and mirrors. Real growth.

remote.title: Researcher
remote.location: Remote — Canada, Germany, Switzerland, United Kingdom, United States
remote.description:
GiveWell’s mission is to help people in need as much as we can by researching the most cost‑effective ways to save and improve lives, sharing our work openly, and directing donations to the programs we believe will do the most good. Our work, which focuses on global health and well-being, is funded by tens of thousands of donors who rely on our research to inform their giving. We’ve grown from directing $1.5 million in 2010 to directing more than $400 million in 2025. We anticipate our total grantmaking is likely to approach or even exceed $1 billion this year, and we are working toward a future that could be several times that scale. Through years of deliberate groundwork, we’ve been growing our research capacity and scope in order to direct substantially more funding to the most impactful opportunities we can find.

Summary
GiveWell is seeking exceptional Researchers to help direct hundreds of millions of dollars annually to the most cost-effective global health and poverty alleviation programs. You’ll have an outsized influence on our funding decisions and help us save and improve lives on a global scale.
You’ll execute ambitious research agendas, answer complex questions, and inform high-impact grantmaking decisions by combining rigorous evidence review, cost-effectiveness modeling, and thoughtful judgment.
Researchers will have the opportunity to develop into Senior Researcher or Senior Program Officer roles, leading research agendas or owning complex grantmaking portfolios. We’re open to a wide variety of professional development options depending on your preferences and our needs.
The role
You’ll join a small grantmaking team to execute ambitious research agendas, sifting through the countless questions we could try to answer and honing in on those that matter most. Your decisions will inform the allocation of hundreds of millions of dollars to dozens of grantees.
Your practical work will combine empirical evidence review, cost-effectiveness modeling, discussions with subject matter experts, and developing your own judgment. In the course of your work, you might approach questions like these:

- What should we believe about the impacts of improved water quality on all-cause mortality?

- What is the impact of building footbridges in rural communities?

- How can we model the general equilibrium effects of cash transfers?

- How should we prioritize programs that reduce poverty relative to programs that reduce deaths?

- How should we think about the opportunity cost of other actors’ contributions to programs we fund?

- How should we account for high levels of uncertainty in our cost-effectiveness estimates?

- How do we use effects from trials conducted 30 to 40 years ago to predict impacts today?

Responsibilities include:

-
Analyzing interventions (e.g., vaccine demand generation, vitamin A supplementation, seasonal malaria chemoprevention) at various levels of depth to refine our view about the cost-effectiveness of a particular intervention and recommend either deprioritization or further work. Researchers review existing empirical evidence about intervention impacts, build models, speak with subject matter experts about particular interventions, and use their judgment to come up with a bottom line. Examples of this work are available on our intervention reports page.

-
Building cost-effectiveness models to estimate the costs and benefits of a particular intervention. These models take into account a wide variety of considerations, including: one's prior estimate for an intervention's impact, the strength of the evidence, the size of the effects, the similarity between the context in which an intervention was studied and will be implemented, negative and/or offsetting effects, and how funding this intervention would affect decisions by other actors (e.g., local government, donor governments). See more on our page about our cost-effectiveness models.

-
Reviewing specific grantmaking opportunities. We receive and solicit requests for funding on an ongoing basis. Researchers investigate each of these opportunities to determine whether or not they should receive funding. Reviewers discuss each grant opportunity with the applying organization, consider its plans and assess the likelihood it will achieve them, estimate the cost-effectiveness of a grant and forecast its likelihood of success. When necessary, they solicit feedback from outside experts (e.g., academics, government officials) about the opportunity.

-
Tackle thorny research questions with creative approaches. We often need to answer questions that don’t have clear answers in published academic journals or other data sources (see some examples above), but which nevertheless matter significantly to our bottom-line funding decisions. You’ll come up with creative approaches to answer these questions, and your work will often influence the funding decisions of many of GiveWell’s research subteams.

-
Building relationships with experts relevant to our work, for example, academics who specialize in interventions we are reviewing (e.g., malaria, malnutrition treatment, in-line water chlorination), leaders and program staff at organizations we are considering for funding, and program staff at foundations who are also evaluating where to allocate funds.

-
Publishing reports and blog posts on our website. Transparency is a core value of ours and we aim to publish as much supporting information regarding our conclusions as we can. Researchers write up our findings and reasoning for publication on our website or summarize key points from their work in blog posts.

What is career development like?
After gaining experience on the team, Researchers have the opportunity to develop into Senior Researchers, who lead the development of our research agendas. Senior Researchers may then pursue a few pathways for career development based on their preferences and GiveWell’s needs. Some choose to develop wider and more autonomous research agendas as individual contributors, while others take on people management responsibilities. Another potential pathway is to transition into a Program Officer or Senior Program Officer position, in which you’d own a high-impact, cost-effective grantmaking portfolios by deepening your expertise, growing your networks, and understanding the broader context within a specific grantmaking area. Senior Program Officers think through questions like:

- How should we balance exploring and seeding new, smaller opportunities with funding cost-effective opportunities at scale today?

- How can we triangulate empirical evidence against expert opinion on other qualitative features, like organizational track record?

- What is research we can fund today that could substantially impact our grantmaking five years from now?

- How much uncertainty are we willing to accept before making a grant? What key research questions do we need to answer before making a grant, and which ones can we deprioritize or answer later?

Team structure
Our research department has ~60 people, and is currently organized into eight teams:

- Five of the teams (Water, Livelihoods, Nutrition, Malaria, and Vaccines) focus on specific areas of grantmaking.

- The New Areas team focuses on interventions in domains that are new to GiveWell.

- The Cross-Cutting team focuses on methodological issues, research quality, and other big-picture concerns that cut across all of our research work.

- The Commons team provides generalized research support to each of the other teams, including landscaping research, vetting, and publishing.

In most cases, we hire Researchers without knowing which subteam they’ll eventually sit on. We aim to expose new researchers to different types of work and parts of the team over several months to inform their eventual subteam placement. (We might settle on a subteam more quickly if new hires bring specific, specialized expertise.)
Team values
We think our research team has unique qualities:

-
We care deeply and centrally about finding and sharing truth. Truth-seeking is one of our core values. We post our mistakes and we prize our team members who keep our culture of free-flowing feedback strong.

-
We are independent. We focus 100% on finding the most cost-effective opportunities to save and improve lives. Our researchers assist in communicating our research findings to the public and our donors, and on occasion we provide tailored advice to ultra-high-net-worth donors who want to rely on our expertise to direct their giving—but we never ask our researchers to trade off against honesty, or to hide their real beliefs.

-
We don’t waste time. Once it’s clear that a particular research question is unlikely to change our bottom-line funding recommendation, we drop it as quickly as possible. We encourage our research staff to constantly re-evaluate their portfolios and only work on the highest-priority questions.

-
Lean research team = huge personal impact. In 2026,our research team of ~80 people is directing close to 1 billion dollars and we expect grantmaking dollars per research team member to increase in the future.

-
We work well together. Our research team is lean because we’re able to attract top-tier people, all of whom complete skills-based assessments before joining our staff. We maintain a high-performing, collegial culture and pay our staff accordingly.

Details

-
Team: You'll join one of our grantmaking teams (see our org structure here) and report to a Senior Researcher or Senior Program Officer.

-
Compensation:

- NYC or the San Francisco Bay Area: $220,000

- All other U.S. locations: $200,000

- International: Similar to the “all other U.S. locations” salary, based on historical exchange rates and delivered in locally-denominated currency.

-
Countries we can hire from: GiveWell is a remote-first organization. However, for the time being, we can only hire within a select number of countries (US, UK, Canada, Switzerland, and Germany). To be considered for a role with GiveWell, you need to already be based in one of those countries or be willing to move to one of them. We expect to expand the list of locations where we can hire over the course of 2027, and our job descriptions always reflect the current status — so we'd encourage you to check back and apply again for a role you're eligible for.

-
Visa sponsorship: The US is the only country where visa sponsorship is possible for a number of roles, and it's assessed on a case by case basis. For all other countries, you need to already have work authorization, we cannot sponsor visas.

-
Why we work this way: Focusing on countries where we already have tested onboarding processes lets us move candidates through hiring faster and with fewer surprises. Every additional country brings its own labor laws, EOR requirements, and new processes to work through, which slows things down for hiring teams and new colleagues alike. Concentrating our footprint keeps the experience consistent and supports GiveWell’s wider absorption capacity goals.

-
Flexibility: We support and encourage flexible working, including flexible hours, working remotely, and working from the office when you choose. The majority of our staff, including senior management, work flexibly in one way or another.

-
Benefits: Our benefits include:

- Fully funded health, dental, vision, and life insurance (we cover 100% of premiums within the US for you and any dependents)

- Four weeks of paid time off per year

- 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave

- Ergonomic home workstations or coworking space memberships

- Automatic contribution equal to 5% of your gross salary into your 403(b) retirement plan (for U.S. based staff)

-
Travel: Research team members are sometimes required to attend international site visits and conferences (on average 1-2 per year), with additional travel for those interested in traveling more. Additionally, we strongly encourage staff members to attend quarterly whole-org and department retreats to bond with other team members and complete in-person work. We'll discuss travel obligations in more detail during late stages of the hiring process, and we’ll accommodate staff who have conflicting family or other obligations.

-
Start date: We’d like a candidate to start as soon as possible after receiving an offer, but we’ll offer flexibility for candidates whose personal or professional circumstances require them to moderately delay their start date.

About you
Our typical hire for this role has a master's degree in a quantitative field (e.g., economics, policy, public health) with a few years of relevant experience, or a PhD in a quantitative field with limited post-graduation experience. We're willing to make exceptions for applicants who don't have advanced degrees but demonstrate equivalent depth of expertise.
We expect you will be characterized by many of the below qualities. We encourage you to apply if you would use the majority of these characteristics to describe yourself:

- You are passionate about helping improve global health and alleviate global poverty as much as possible.

- You are highly skilled at critically analyzing and synthesizing empirical research and understanding how a body of evidence may apply to real-world problems.

- You are able to plan an efficient approach to exploring complicated questions, including identifying and focusing on the most decision-relevant aspects of a project.

- You consider the big picture, asking questions like: is this project appropriately formulated and the best use of my time? What is GiveWell getting wrong in our research?

- You clearly communicate what you believe and why, as well as what you are uncertain about.

- You ask a lot of questions, and are curious, rather than defensive, when interrogating your own or others’ work.

- You are able to execute research that holds up under scrutiny from others and over time.

- You are respectful, effective, and efficient in your interactions with colleagues as well as external parties.

Other notes

- Please note that our hiring process consists of the same work trials for the following roles: Researcher, Senior Researcher, Senior Cross-Cutting Researcher, Senior Livelihoods Researcher, Senior Malaria Researcher, Senior New Areas Researcher, Senior Nutrition Researcher, Senior Vaccination Researcher, and Senior Water Researcher. If, within the last year, you applied and were rejected for one of these roles, you should hold off on applying to the other roles, unless explicitly asked to do so by a member of our team. If you're interested in all of these roles, please just apply once and note in your application that you'd like to be considered for the other roles, too.

- Please note that this role was previously titled "Senior Research Associate." The position itself remains unchanged.

- After application review, our hiring process consists of a short application exercise, two compensated work trials, and several short interviews. You can see more details about our hiring process on our FAQs page!

- You don't need to submit a cover letter with your application—we only want your resume/CV and answers to the application questions below.

- Economics PhD candidates on the job market do not need a job market paper to apply.

- We don’t offer informational calls at this stage, but please email us at with any questions not answered here!

About GiveWell

GiveWell is dedicated to finding and evaluating highly cost-effective global health and development opportunities, and we publish all the work, reasoning, and uncertainties behind our funding decisions. Our giving funds enable donors to contribute to the most impactful and cost-effective programs our researchers identify.

GiveWell is one of the world’s largest private funders of global development efforts. Trusted annually by tens of thousands of donors, GiveWell searches for highly cost-effective programs that save or improve lives the most. Since 2007, more than 150,000 donors have given over $2.6 billion through GiveWell to the most promising programs its research has identified, which we estimate will save more than 340,000 lives.

GiveWell is most well-known for recommending a small number of Top Charities, which currently support seasonal malaria chemoprevention, insecticide-treated nets, vaccine incentivization, and vitamin A supplementation. However, most of our research capacity and grantmaking is devoted to cost-effective opportunities outside of those programs.

GiveWell grants have:

- Helped governments navigate changes to the funding landscape and implement high-impact health programs, like HIV/syphilis screening and treatment for pregnant people in Zambia and Cameroon.

- Sought to scope and scale promising interventions that don’t have clear existing implementers. We are supporting the Clinton Health Access Initiative’s Incubator to identify potentially cost-effective interventions and create programs that we would be excited to support in the future. For example, we funded a program to prevent tuberculosis among young children in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, India, that we co-designed with CHAI through the Incubator program.

- Provided funding to ensure that programs that recently faced foreign aid funding cuts could continue, like healthcare support and malnutrition treatment in northern Cameroon.

- Funded program delivery alongside strengthened monitoring and evaluation, as in our grants to support treatment of clubfoot and to evaluate the program.

- Tested our assumptions and refined our understanding through further research and data collection, including improved estimates of disease burden and studies on the effect of water chlorination on mortality and the impact of a tree-planting program on farmers’ income.

We make our reasoning public and transparent so others can challenge it (sometimes we even pay people to point out our errors). We go to unusual lengths to check our assumptions and assess our impact, including funding research to address our uncertainties and gathering independent monitoring and evaluation data about the programs we support. We change our minds when the evidence demands it. For more about GiveWell, listen to Ezra Klein’s recent interview with GiveWell’s co-founder and CEO Elie Hassenfeld.

Additional information

We don’t want to miss candidates that could do great things at GiveWell. Practically, that means a GiveWell staff member reviews every application carefully, considering the whole picture of your background and potential. If you’re on the fence about applying because you meet some but not 100% of our preferred qualifications (some studies suggest this hesitation is especially common for women and people of color), we encourage you to apply anyway.

GiveWell is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer by choice. At minimum, this means that we comply with all federal, state, and local EEO and employment laws. Beyond the requirements of those laws, we value our team’s diversity in all respects, and we desire to maintain a work environment free of harassment or discrimination—we want our team members to thrive at GiveWell. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, contact us at . We will consider employment for qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

By submitting an application, you acknowledge that you have read and consent to GiveWell's Privacy Statement for Applicants. By completing an application exercise, you acknowledge and assent to GiveWell's Work Trial Policy.

remote.description:
About BJAK
The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.
The Role
We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead a high-performing engineering team building and scaling products used by millions of users across the region.
This role is for a strong technical leader who can lead engineers, make sound architecture and engineering decisions, and drive products and systems from idea to production. You will be responsible for both the quality of the engineering team and the quality and speed of what the team ships.
You should be comfortable operating across people, product and technology — setting a high engineering bar while keeping the team focused on delivering real customer and business outcomes.
What You'll Own

- Lead and manage a team of engineers across frontend, backend and full stack development.

- Own engineering delivery for major product areas, ensuring the team ships quickly without compromising reliability and technical quality.

- Work closely with product, design, mobile, backend and AI teams to turn ambiguous product problems into clear technical execution.

- Drive technical architecture and engineering decisions across APIs, databases, integrations, infrastructure and customer-facing systems.

- Set engineering standards around code quality, system design, testing, observability, security and production reliability.

- Stay close to the technical work through architecture reviews, code reviews, debugging and critical engineering decisions.

- Develop engineers through regular feedback, coaching, performance management and clear expectations.

- Identify performance gaps early and take ownership of raising the team's engineering and execution bar.

- Improve engineering processes, tooling and automation to help the team move faster and operate at scale.

- Own production outcomes beyond release: monitor systems, resolve incidents, identify root causes and ensure problems do not repeat.

- Build a strong engineering culture focused on ownership, speed, technical excellence and continuous improvement.

What We're Looking For

- Strong software engineering background with experience building and shipping real production systems.

- Experience leading or managing software engineers and owning engineering delivery.

- Strong technical depth across backend, frontend, APIs, databases, distributed systems or cloud infrastructure.

- Able to make sound architecture and technical trade-offs while balancing speed, scalability and maintainability.

- Strong track record of taking products or systems from idea through development, launch and production.

- Comfortable reviewing technical designs, challenging engineering decisions and debugging complex production issues.

- Strong people leadership with the ability to coach engineers, manage performance and build high-performing teams.

- Strong product sense and ability to connect engineering decisions to customer and business outcomes.

- Able to work fast with ambiguity, establish priorities and drive teams toward clear outcomes.

- Strong ownership mentality — when something breaks or delivery slips, you take responsibility for getting it back on track.

This Role Is Not For

- Managers who want to manage people without staying close to the technology.

- Engineers who want the title of Engineering Manager but do not want accountability for team performance.

- Leaders who need complete specifications before their team can start.

- Managers who measure success by meetings, processes or tickets instead of shipped outcomes.

- People who avoid difficult technical decisions, performance conversations or production issues.

- Candidates who make vague leadership claims without being able to explain what they personally built, led, improved or scaled.

The Bar
We are looking for engineering leaders with real technology career highlights.
A strong highlight is not just managing a large team or working at a famous company. A strong highlight means you personally helped build, ship or scale a serious product, platform or engineering organisation and can clearly explain your contribution.
You should be able to demonstrate both sides of engineering leadership: technical depth and the ability to build a high-performing team that consistently delivers.
Location
This is a remote role. We hire globally and work across multiple countries and time zones.
Candidates should be comfortable working effectively in a distributed, fast-moving international team and collaborating with colleagues across different locations.
Language
English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.
Interview Process
Our process is designed to move fast:

- Online assessment or practical task

- Technical / engineering leadership interview

- CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

remote.title: AIOps & Agentic Operations Advisory Senior Manager
remote.description:
Accenture is a global professional services company with leading capabilities in digital, cloud and security. Combining unmatched experience and specialized skills across more than 40 industries, we offer Strategy and, Interactive, Technology, and Operations services, all powered by the world’s largest network of Advanced Technology and Intelligent Operations centers. Our 738,000 people deliver on the promise of technology and human ingenuity every day, serving clients in more than 120 countries. We embrace the power of change to create value and shared success for our clients, people, shareholders, partners, and communities. Visit us at .
We are seeking an experienced Senior Manager, AIOps & Agentic Operations Advisory to help large enterprises move from reactive, human-run operations to intelligent, automation-first delivery. This role is built for practitioners who have actually run enterprise IT operations at scale — and who now bring that hard-won experience to bear in designing the AIOps and agentic operating models that will replace much of what they once managed manually. The value this person brings is not theoretical: they know what breaks, what matters at 2am, and where automation genuinely changes outcomes versus where it creates new risk. They translate that grounded perspective into a compelling vision for CIO audiences and into delivery plans that cross-functional teams can execute.
The Work:

- Design AIOps and agentic operations architectures grounded in real enterprise run experience — identifying where autonomous operations genuinely reduce risk and cost, and where human judgment must be preserved

- Frame the vision for CIO audiences — translating complex operational transformation into a clear business case, articulating the path from current-state operations to an automation-first, agentic target state

- Build the delivery plans — defining phased roadmaps, workstream structures, tooling selections, and operating model transitions that delivery teams can own and execute without the advisory lead needing to run each workstream

- Assess and sequence the automation opportunity — applying operations experience to distinguish genuine quick wins from automation that looks good in a slide but fails in production, and prioritising accordingly

- Lead the operating model transition — redesigning roles, processes, and governance for a world where agents handle event triage, remediation, and change execution, and human operators focus on exception handling, oversight, and continuous improvement

- Shape and support business development — leading client workshops, originating opportunities through peer-to-peer CIO engagement, and contributing to proposals where operations credibility is the differentiator

- Provide thought leadership on the frontiers of intelligent operations — including multi-agent orchestration, AI-driven change risk assessment, autonomous remediation guardrails, and the governance frameworks needed to operate at machine speed

Travel may be required for this role. The amount of travel will vary from 25% to 100% depending on business need and client requirements.

- Minimum 8+ years of progressive experience in IT operations, infrastructure engineering, or technology consulting — with a meaningful portion spent actually running enterprise operations at scale, not only advising on them

- Minimum 8+ years in a leadership role with accountability for operational performance, service delivery, or infrastructure reliability in a complex enterprise environment

- Minimum 3+ years experience designing and delivering AIOps, automation, or intelligent operations programs — with evidence of measurable operational outcomes (MTTR reduction, automation coverage, alert noise reduction, toil elimination)

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent (minimum 12 years) work experience. (If Associate’s Degree, must have minimum 6 years work experience)

Bonus Points If:

- Prior experience in a senior enterprise operations role (Head of IT Operations, VP Infrastructure, NOC Director, or equivalent) before moving into consulting or advisory — the practitioner-to-advisor career path is a strong signal for this position

- Hands-on experience deploying or operating AIOps tooling in production (Dynatrace, Moogsoft, BigPanda, PagerDuty, Datadog, or equivalent) — not only designing or evaluating it

- Experience in regulated industries (financial services, energy, life sciences, public sector) where autonomous operations require additional governance, audit trails, and human oversight controls

- Industry certifications in cloud operations, SRE, or AIOps platforms; familiarity with ITIL 4 and how its practices adapt in an automation-first operating model

Skills:

- AIOps & Intelligent Ops Design: Hybrid/multi-cloud AIOps platform design (noise reduction, anomaly detection), agentic operations (autonomous triage, self-healing runbooks), and unified telemetry observability (Dynatrace, Datadog, Splunk, OpenTelemetry).

- Enterprise Operations Credibility: Hands-on background leading NOC/SOC and major incident command, navigating operational realities (alert fatigue, change freezes), and driving SRE/reliability practices (SLO/SLI frameworks, error budgets).

- Automation-First Delivery: End-to-end automation programme design (ROI modeling, toolchain selection), actionable workstream architecture, and organizational change/adoption management for human oversight of AI workflows.

- Executive Advisory & Thought Leadership: CIO-level strategic vision and business case development, alongside grounded points of view on agentic AI readiness and phased adoption roadmap sequencing.

- Aligning Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance around clear product decisions and launch requirements.

- Strong technical foundation across system architecture, APIs, databases, workflows, failure modes and distributed systems.

- Experience working closely with engineers and ability to review, challenge and contribute to technical designs.

- Experience in payments, banking, remittance, insurance, trading or another regulated, high-consequence product domain.

- Strong product judgment and ability to make difficult trade-offs under technical, regulatory and operational constraints.

- Experience building with LLMs or AI products, including evaluation, reliability and understanding when AI should not be used.

Nice to have

- Engineering or highly technical product background.

- Experience building zero-to-one fintech or consumer products.

- Experience defining evaluation frameworks for ML or LLM-powered products.

- Ships fast and clears the gates that actually block launch

- Money is correct and users are never misled about the state of their funds

- AI features are valuable, predictable and trusted

- Engineering, design, compliance, and operations are aligned with minimal friction

At Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people. We’re a global close-knit community, united by the relentless pursuit to help keep people safer everywhere. We build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and places. Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Motorola Solutions is a recognized global leader in Enterprise Security & Resilience software, offering a next-generation cloud platform that empowers organizations to navigate risks, disruptions, and crises with confidence. Our technology unifies critical functions — risk intelligence, security operations, crisis & emergency management, and business continuity — into a single, powerful platform.

We are building the "digital brain" of the modern Security Operations Center (SOC). While competitors focus on better detection, our platform automates the decision loop. We are seeking a product leader to define the future of Agentic AI in physical security—moving the industry from reactive monitoring to proactive, automated resilience.

You will own the roadmap for a new cloud-native intelligence platform that unifies video, access control, and critical communications. As well as automating detection and verification, its agents augment SOC teams through proactive coordination of security incident responses, orchestrating devices and inputs at scale whilst collaborating with human operators.

In this role, you’ll take ownership across the full product lifecycle — shaping strategy, engaging with customers, driving execution, and delivering product features that lead the market. You’ll collaborate closely with senior management, fellow product managers, UX designers, engineering, sales, customer success, and professional services teams to shape and deliver best-in-class product experiences.
You’ll be responsible for engaging directly with customers and sales people, and researching and analysing the market and competitors, to drive the creation of differentiated value in your product. You will gather and prioritize product ideas, maintain strategic roadmaps, and define requirements and features. You will work closely with our engineering, AI and UX teams to drive feature design and development. The ideal candidate is a creative and strategic thinker, a collaborative product manager with experience in visual AI, and with excellent UX design instincts.

Calendar Management

- Apply calendar standard work consistently, including accurate attendees and reporting relationships, agendas, pre-reads, links and locations, global time zones and appropriate meeting buffers; flag overloaded days or competing priorities and recommend adjustments.

Job Readiness

Workflow Support

- Coordinate leadership meetings, town halls, offsites and other important team moments, including objectives, agendas, participants, materials, logistics and next steps.

- Track decisions, commitments and follow-ups, carry forward prior direction and close loops with clear owners and deadlines.

- Build strong relationships across the leadership team and broader organization so you understand what is happening, connect related work and know when something needs the CMO’s attention.

Executive Operation Support

- Plan domestic and international travel, including itineraries, hotels, transportation, meeting logistics, contingency plans and expense reports.

- Manage incoming requests and correspondence, prepare and quality-check presentations, emails, reports and meeting materials, and route questions to the right people.

- Handle confidential business, talent and personal information with discretion, and bring warmth, professionalism and a sense of humor to a fast-moving global team.

Requirements

- At least 10 years of experience as an Executive Assistant supporting senior executives in a complex, global business environment; experience supporting a leader responsible for a multibillion-dollar business or portfolio is strongly preferred.

- Strong business judgment and calendar-management skills, with the ability to connect the executive’s time to business priorities—not simply who asked first or where there is an open slot.

- Forward-looking and proactive: you naturally scan the horizon, anticipate preparation needs, identify the right stakeholders and act before being prompted.

- Curious about the business and the marketing function, with the ability to learn the portfolio, people, planning cycles and operating rhythms quickly.

- A clear communicator and trusted relationship builder who can gather context across the organization, use discretion and know when to act, escalate or ask a question.

- Highly organized and dependable, with the speed, accuracy and attention to detail needed to manage changing priorities and consistently apply standard work.
